item.title: Can Rays rebound from 0-2 World Series deficit? Here's some inspiration
item.description: The Tampa Bay Rays face a tall order after losing the first two games of the 2026 World Series to the Milwaukee Brewers . As they prepare for Game 3 on Monday, Oct. 26 at home, the Rays will look to do something no team this century has accomplished: come back from an 0-2 deficit to win the World Series . The last team to pull off such a comeback was the 1996 New York Yankees , who dropped the first two games to the Atlanta Braves, but then stormed back to win the next four in a row and kick off a dominant run of four titles in five seasons. The Rays would love to add their name to a very short list. In the 121-year history of the World Series, only 10 teams have successfully managed to pull off an 0-2 comeback. Which teams have come back from 0-2 to win World Series? The Rays and Brewers have been called "throwback teams" this postseason for their reliance on some old-school principles − such as bunting, base-stealing and defensive excellence − that seem to have fallen out of favor in the power-heavy modern game. If the Rays need some inspiration for their comeback, they can point to three teams in the decidedly old-school 1980s who did rebound from losing the first two games to win the World Series. Down (0-2), but not out 1996 New York Yankees (def. Atlanta Braves 4-2) 1986 New York Mets (def. Boston Red Sox 4-3) 1985 Kansas City Royals (def. St. Louis Cardinals 4-3) 1981 Los Angeles Dodgers (def. New York Yankees 4-2) 1978 New York Yankees (def. Los Angeles Dodgers 4-2) 1971 Pittsburgh Pirates (def. Baltimore Orioles 4-3) 1965 Los Angeles Dodgers (def. Minnesota Twins 4-3) 1958 New York Yankees (def. Milwaukee Braves 4-3) 1956 New York Yankees (def. Brooklyn Dodgers 4-3) 1955 Brooklyn Dodgers (def. New York Yankees 4-3) This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Can Rays rebound from 0-2 World Series deficit? Here's some inspiration

item.title: Seedy K’s Pigskin Palaver: Mystery Endings
item.description: I stream a lot of murder mysteries. British. Scandinavian. Mostly. For my taste, they are a bit more sophisticated. Generally speaking more cerebral, less gore. But, hey, everybody’s taste is different. If you prefer grizzly, have at it. All are full of MacGuffins. This guy did it. No, it was her. What a sec, what about . . .? So, I always look for the character who is in a scene or two early on. Of no consequence . . . we think. Until the final episode, when we learn he or she or them is/ are the perp(s). Usually out of nowhere. In the better series, it makes sense. In many, the plot maneuvers are so convoluted, you’re left with mixed feelings. Which brings me to this past week in college pigskin. Dead Man Walking List Culled. Pop Quiz. The first one who can name where Mike Locksley coaches — er, coached — wins a tip of the hat. Point is he’s the first coach canned this in season.* Like those mystery perps, we didn’t see it coming, that he’d be first. Maybe after the team’s last game. He was the first of three. Joing him in the stands not along the sideline: After thirteen and a half seasons of mediocrity, NC State finally pinkslipped Dave Doeren. Why now, and not after the Worst Ever Last Play L to Vandy? Baylor’s Dave Aranda became the next one to bite the dust. While Mike Norvell, the consensus top pick, the guy all clues pointed to, the guy we all have been expecting to put up a For Sale sign, still wears the headset. *Locksley coached at Maryland, as inconsequential as you can get. Hollywood Busts. You know how every so often you see a young actor in a movie in a minor role and they just about steal the whole movie. They become The Next Big Thing in Tinseltown. Like, oh, Mickey Rourke, after his breakout as the very philosophical arsonist Teddy Lewis In “Body Heat”.* Then Boogie in “Diner.” *We also met young Ted Danson in that one as the DA. Well, Rourke has had a long career, but Not Quite What Was Expected after that early charismatic promise. He’s 6-2 this year, but the celsius of his seat is on the increase after getting waxed at Camp Randall. Mormons Book It. Central Florida’s victory over Brigham Young was so absurd, so full of what happened there moments, I won’t even try to explain. Points given back. Weird calls. Big plays. Big miscues. item.title: Smotherman beats Power in Monday finish in Bermuda
item.description: Smotherman prevailed on the third extra hole to secure back-to-back PGA Tour wins [Getty Images] Austin Smotherman claimed his second PGA Tour title with a Monday play-off victory over Seamus Power at the weather-hit Bermuda Championship. The 32-year-old American parred the third extra hole to fend off the Irishman and seal his second tournament win in as many starts after a breakthrough victory in Utah earlier this month. Smotherman and Power contested the sudden-death play-off on Monday after inclement weather forced organisers to cancel Sunday's scheduled final round. With more bad weather forecast on Monday, officials decided to scrap the final round and proceed with a play-off between the 54-hole leaders. Smotherman carded 65, 66 and 66 to reach 16 under through three rounds, with 2022 champion Power matching his 197 total with rounds of 66, 64 and 67. On the first play-off hole - the par-three 16th at Port Royal Golf Course - Power missed a 20-footer for his third PGA Tour win before getting up and down from the bunker to force a third extra hole. With the hole location having been changed, Smotherman two-putted from 15 feet for the win after Power failed to get up and down for par from the rough. "We're out here playing an incredible sport in a beautiful spot," said Smotherman. "Whatever things are going to be thrown at us, Zak [Williamson, caddie] and I were going to be on top of our game. "Yesterday I felt like we handled everything pretty well and the tour has been great at communicating what's going to happen today for us. "Once we got that news, it was nice to know what's going on. To come out on top is a cherry on top, so it's pretty awesome." While Power missed out on the trophy, the runner-up finish effectively guarantees his PGA Tour card for 2027 after playing with conditional status this year. Having entered the week 103rd in the FedEx Cup Fall standings, the 39-year-old is projected to climb to 53rd, with the top 100 earning PGA Tour cards for next year. "Had a chance this morning, wasn't able to do it, which is disappointing, but overall great week, can't complain too much," said Power. "Hit some good shots in the playoff, just didn't quite judge the wind right, but that's golf sometimes. I'll move onwards."

item.title: Texas football film review: Longhorns can't recover an onside kick. Who's to blame?
item.description: Mississippi Rebels safety Andy Jaffe recovers an onside kick in the fourth quarter against the Texas Longhorns at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday Oct. 24, 2026. (Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman) Texas football has two wins in SEC play after Saturday's 34-27 triumph over Ole Miss . Both victories were nearly fumbled away thanks to a recurring headache for Steve Sarkisian 's squad. The Longhorns secured their latest victory on the final play of regulation at Royal-Memorial Stadium, a Hail Mary attempt from Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss intercepted by Longhorns defensive back Jelani McDonald. The heart-stopping heave ended in a clutch play from Texas' defense. It followed another frustrating gaffe for Texas' special teams unit, in which the Longhorns allowed Ole Miss to recover an onside kick with 1:15 remaining. OLE MISS RECOVERS THE ONSIDE KICK FROM TEXAS OMG 🤯 https://t.co/093ft8L0w9 - ESPN (@espn) October 25, 2026 Have déjà vu, Texas fans? Your memory doesn't deceive you. The Longhorns' 20-17 win at Tennessee last month ended on a Hail Mary pass from Volunteers quarterback Faizon Brandon that landed incomplete. That incompletion came four plays after a Tennessee onside kick attempt, which was then recovered by the Volunteers. OLE MISS RECOVERS THE ONSIDE KICK FROM TEXAS OMG 🤯 https://t.co/093ft8L0w9 - ESPN (@espn) October 25, 2026 Were Texas' pair of late-game gaffes unfortunate miscues, or is there a larger issue at play? We checked the film to find out. Breaking down Texas onside kick struggles Texas' struggles on offense or defense need a close examination to properly diagnose. That's not the case with Texas' onside kick failures. See the pair of images below. Texas is in proper position to recover both onside kicks against Ole Miss and Tennessee, with a wide receiver ready to receive the ball without an opponent within three yards. The same error then befell Texas twice. Wide receiver Ryan Wingo attempted to field the onside kick at Tennessee, but a skipping football flew under his arms, hit him in the chest and sprayed behind him toward midfield. Fellow wideout Emmett Mosley V was the designated onside-kick receiver against Ole Miss, but the ball hit him in the chest after a third hop before shooting into the air. Both plays ended in clear recoveries for Texas opponents. Both created frantic finishes in what should have been tidy wins. Texas football failed to recover an onside kick for the second time in four weeks in a win over Ole Miss on Saturday, October 24, 2026. (via Youtube) Texas football gave Tennessee a second life in the final minutes when it failed to recover an onside kick in the fourth quarter on Saturday, September 26, 2026. (via Youtube) Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said postgame Saturday he had no problem with the design of Texas' onside-kick recovery. The issue came from the Longhorns' poor execution. That's not the case with Texas' onside kick failures. See the pair of images below. Texas is in proper position to recover both onside kicks against Ole Miss and Tennessee, with a wide receiver ready to receive the ball without an opponent within three yards. Wide receiver Ryan Wingo attempted to field the onside kick at Tennessee, but a skipping football flew under his arms, hit him in the chest and sprayed behind him toward midfield. Texas football failed to recover an onside kick for the second time in four weeks in a win over Ole Miss on Saturday, October 24, 2026. (via Youtube) Texas football gave Tennessee a second life in the final minutes when it failed to recover an onside kick in the fourth quarter on Saturday, September 26, 2026. (via Youtube) Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said postgame Saturday he had no problem with the design of Texas' onside-kick recovery. The issue came from the Longhorns' poor execution. "I don't know if there's, like, [a] fix special teams," Sarkisian said. "We didn't field the ball on an onside kick. It wasn't like they had a free runner and they just got the ball, but we dropped it twice and they got it. That's human error." Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian talks to an offical in the fourth quarter against the Mississippi Rebels at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday Oct. 24, 2026. (Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman) Glaring gaffes Texas' coaches can chalk the pair of botched onside kicks to human error. But those two plays aren't isolated incidents for Texas' special-terms unit, an increasingly criticized group under special teams coordinator Jeff Banks. Texas allowed a blocked punt that resulted in an Oklahoma touchdown in this year's Red River Rivalry loss to the Sooners. Florida generated 105 kick-return yards in a win in Austin the next week, and the Longhorns paired Saturday's onside-kick error with two personal-foul penalties on special-teams plays from freshman linebacker Kosi Okpala. The Longhorns sport one of college football's most expensive rosters. Banks is reportedly the sport's most expensive offensive coordinator with a $1.2 million annual salary. His unit isn't living up to the billing through four SEC games, hindering a Texas team clinging to its College Football Playoff hopes. item.title: The biggest Ballon d'Or controversies 😡
item.description: The biggest Ballon d'Or controversies 😡 The Ballon d'Or has had its fair share of controversies. This Monday evening, the Ballon d'Or ceremony will take place live from London. One thing is certain: with no clear favourite, the result will get people talking around the world. To mark the occasion, we're taking a look back at the biggest controversies in the history of this prestigious award. Haaland snubbed despite an outstanding season In 2023, Erling Haaland was coming off an extraordinary season with Manchester City. He scored 52 goals in 53 matches and played a major role in the club's historic treble, which included a Champions League triumph, while also setting the record for goals in a single Premier League season (35). Despite those impressive numbers, Lionel Messi won the Ballon d'Or, largely thanks to his World Cup triumph with Argentina. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner even finished more than 100 votes ahead of his Norwegian rival. Sneijder only fourth in 2010 Wesley Sneijder had an exceptional 2010. With Inter Milan, he won the Champions League and several other trophies before reaching the World Cup final with the Netherlands. Yet he finished only fourth in the voting, behind Messi, Iniesta and Xavi. That fourth-place finish remains one of the biggest anomalies in the award's history, especially given his pivotal role in Inter's success and the Netherlands' World Cup run. Thierry Henry snubbed in 2003 Thierry Henry finished second in the 2003 Ballon d'Or behind Pavel Nedvěd. Yet the Frenchman was coming off a historic season with Arsenal, becoming the first player in Premier League history to record more than 20 goals and 20 assists in a single campaign. Many therefore felt that Henry could, or even should, have won the award. Still, Nedvěd deserves credit for winning Serie A and reaching the Champions League final that year, despite posting less impressive numbers than the Frenchman. Real Madrid's fury in 2024 Rodri's victory in 2024 sparked huge controversy. Vinícius Jr. was widely seen as the favourite following his performances for Real Madrid, particularly in the Champions League. But Rodri received the award after an exceptional season with Manchester City and, above all, after winning the Euros with Spain and being named the tournament's best player. After learning just hours before the award presentation that Vinícius Jr. had lost, the entire Real Madrid delegation decided to boycott the ceremony. That boycott continued the following year, although the Madrid contingent is expected to return for Monday evening's ceremony. With Inter Milan, he won the Champions League and several other trophies before reaching the World Cup final with the Netherlands. Yet he finished only fourth in the voting, behind Messi, Iniesta and Xavi. That fourth-place finish remains one of the biggest anomalies in the award's history, especially given his pivotal role in Inter's success and the Netherlands' World Cup run. Thierry Henry snubbed in 2003 Thierry Henry finished second in the 2003 Ballon d'Or behind Pavel Nedvěd. Yet the Frenchman was coming off a historic season with Arsenal, becoming the first player in Premier League history to record more than 20 goals and 20 assists in a single campaign. Many therefore felt that Henry could, or even should, have won the award. Still, Nedvěd deserves credit for winning Serie A and reaching the Champions League final that year, despite posting less impressive numbers than the Frenchman. Real Madrid's fury in 2024 Rodri's victory in 2024 sparked huge controversy. Vinícius Jr. was widely seen as the favourite following his performances for Real Madrid, particularly in the Champions League. But Rodri received the award after an exceptional season with Manchester City and, above all, after winning the Euros with Spain and being named the tournament's best player. After learning just hours before the award presentation that Vinícius Jr. had lost, the entire Real Madrid delegation decided to boycott the ceremony. That boycott continued the following year, although the Madrid contingent is expected to return for Monday evening's ceremony. The deadline change that favoured Ronaldo The 2013 edition was particularly controversial. Cristiano Ronaldo had an exceptional year individually, but won no major team trophies with Real Madrid. Meanwhile, Franck Ribéry was among the favourites thanks to Bayern Munich's historic treble as they swept aside the competition across Europe. However, the voting period was unexpectedly extended, allowing the 2014 World Cup play-offs to be taken into account. Ronaldo then delivered a spectacular performance against Sweden, scoring four goals across the two matches, while the Frenchman struggled against Ukraine and saw Karim Benzema and Mamadou Sakho emerge as France's heroes. The Portuguese star eventually won the trophy ahead of Messi and Ribéry, fuelling debate over the impact of the deadline change. Lewandowski: the biggest robbery in history? The biggest controversy is probably still that of 2020. In the midst of the COVID-19 pandemic, France Football decided not to award the Ballon d'Or that year. The biggest loser was Robert Lewandowski, who had an exceptional individual season and won the treble with Bayern Munich Six years later, many observers still consider the decision not to award the prize one of the greatest injustices in modern football, given how certain the Polish striker seemed to win it. The following year, while accepting his seventh Ballon d'Or, Lionel Messi even publicly acknowledged that Robert Lewandowski should have won the previous year. item.title: What channel is Penn State football vs Purdue? Time, TV, streaming
item.description: Penn State football will try to earn its first victory in more than a month on Saturday, Oct. 31, in Beaver Stadium . Yes, these Nittany Lions under first-year head coach Matt Campbell have not celebrated in a postgame locker room since Sept. 19. Four Big Ten tests and four surprising defeats, in one fashion or another. So, how promising does the streak-breaking opportunity appear against the Purdue Boilermakers (3-4, 2-2 Big Ten) on Halloween? Despite their issues , the Lions are still favored to earn that elusive first league victory against an opponent with one of the weakest defenses around. That could prove to be a welcoming salve. item.title: The 1 thing Roquan Smith needs Ravens to chase after meltdown vs. Bengals
item.description: Peter Casey-Imagn Images The 1 thing Roquan Smith needs Ravens to chase after meltdown vs. Bengals appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Baltimore Ravens suffered a monumental collapse against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday night. After going up 13-0, the Ravens gave up 35 unanswered points in the second half to go down to 4-3 on the season. It’s the second such collapse the Ravens have suffered in as many games. They had a similar meltdown in a 13-10 loss to the Cleveland Browns. Amid another demoralizing defeat, Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith wants the team to find the consistency in their performances . “It’s about chasing that consistency and finding that missing piece to where that consistency that we’re chasing, there’s something in there that’s missing. But it’s obviously there a lot, but it’s not there all the time. So there’s finding that, and chasing that, play in and play out, quarter in and quarter out, regardless of the circumstances, and being detached from the result,” Smith said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Despite missing starting quarterback Lamar Jackson once again, the Ravens have been playing quite well to start games with Tyler Huntley. However, for some reason, they are unable to carry that over to the second half, which has led to their collapses. Obviously, the return of the two-time NFL MVP would help solve a lot of those concerns. But the entire team, including Smith and the defense, needs to take accountability for these collapses. There needs to be more consistency with how they play in order to avoid experiencing more meltdowns. The Ravens will be keen to avoid a third straight defeat when they pay a visit to Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills next week. Related: Trey Hendrickson urges Ravens to meet ‘standard’ after getting torched by his old team Related: What Jesse Minter said about truly appalling collapse vs. Bengals that should have Ravens questioning everything

Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Michael Carrick's is seemingly on the verge of being dismissed as Manchester United manager after nine months in charge at Old Trafford. The former Spurs, United and England midfielder got the role on a permanent basis after leading the Red Devils to a third-place finish and Champions League football, but their form has fallen apart this term. Sunday's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth extended their winless run to eight matches across all competitions and United are languishing 16th in the Premier League table. item.content:encoded: Man United managers since Sir Alex Ferguson: Best record, stats with Michael Carrick on the brink originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Michael Carrick's is seemingly on the verge of being dismissed as Manchester United manager after nine months in charge at Old Trafford. Carrick oversaw a dramatic improvement after he replaced Ruben Amorim in January, initially on a short-term deal until the end of the season. The former Spurs, United and England midfielder got the role on a permanent basis after leading the Red Devils to a third-place finish and Champions League football, but their form has fallen apart this term. Sunday's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth extended their winless run to eight matches across all competitions and United are languishing 16th in the Premier League table. Carrick is United's ninth manager since Sir Alex Ferguson left Old Trafford in 2013. Here is how his record stacks up. MORE: Man United 0-3 Bournemouth as it happened | What Bruno Fernandes said about Michael Carrick's tactics Man United managers since Alex Ferguson compared Appointed Sacked Played Won Drawn Lost Win % Trophies won David Moyes July 1, 2013 April 22, 2014 51 26 10 15 50.98% 2014 Community Shield Louis van Gaal July 16, 2014 May 23, 2016 103 54 24 25 52.43% 2015/16 FA Cup Jose Mourinho May 27, 2016 December 18, 2018 144 84 31 29 58.33% 2016 Community Shield, 2016/17 Carabao Cup, 2016/17 UEFA Europa League Ole Gunnar Solskjaer December 18, 2019 November 21, 2021 168 92 35 41 54.76% _ Ralf Rangnick December 3, 2021 May 22, 2022 29 11 9 9 39.93% _ Erik ten Hag May 23, 2022 October 28, 2024 128 72 20 36 56.25% 2022/23 Carabao Cup, 2023/24 FA Cup Ruben Amorim November 11, 2024 January 5, 2026 63 24 18 21 38.1% _ Michael Carrick January 13, 2024 _ 29 14 7 8 48.28% _ Record of Man United managers since Sir Alex Ferguson Below is a breakdown of all the managers to have taken charge of Manchester United since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in May 2013, listed in chronological order. Ryan Giggs and Darren Fletcher are omitted, as they were only briefly appointed as caretakers. The same applies to Carrick's caretaker spell between the tenures of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Ralf Rangnick. David Moyes Ferguson's "Chosen One" soon had that weighty moniker used against him, but things did not start badly. United won the Community Shield against Wigan Athletic and thrashed Swansea City 4-1 in their opening Premier League game. "Come on David Moyes, play like Fergie's boys…" Only they couldn't keep it up. A 1-0 defeat to Liverpool at Anfield and an emphatic 4-1 derby loss away to Manchester City shortly afterwards were blows from which Moyes' United never really recovered. Humiliating 3-0 defeats to both of those bitter rivals at Old Trafford in March 2014 left the Scot hanging by a thread and his former club Everton applied the final blow at a baying Goodison Park, ending Moyes' tenure within the first season of a six-year contract. David Moyes Man United record : P51 W26 D10 L15 (50.98% win percentage) Louis van Gaal With the continuity-candidate plan in tatters, United made their first post-Fergie pitch for a major player in the global game with the gravitas to fill Sir Alex's shoes. Hopes were high around Van Gaal after he led the Netherlands to third place at the 2014 FIFA World Cup. A largely assured start at Old Trafford was torpedoed by a crazy 5-3 defeat to a Jamie Vardy-inspired Leicester City . From that result onwards, there was an overly prosaic emphasis in Van Gaal's United sides, with marquee signing Angel Di Maria and Robin van Persie among those whose influence rapidly declined. Things seemed to have clicked during a spring 2015 run when Liverpool and City were authoritatively dispatched and United returned to the Champions League. But despite the emergence of Marcus Rashford, United could not kick on in the 2015/16 season when they finished sixth as Leicester were crowned champions. An FA Cup final win over Crystal Palace could not save Van Gaal, because one of the biggest names in the sport was on the market at that time. Louis van Gaal Man United record : Pl03 W54 D24 L25 (52.43% win percentage) Getty Images Jose Mourinho The stage was set for the next instalment of Mourinho's rivalry with Pep Guardiola following the thrills and spills across El Clasico's divide from half a decade earlier. Manchester City's assured early-season derby win at Old Trafford gave an early indication of where part two might be heading, although Mourinho emerged from his first season with credit in the bank. Despite only finishing sixth as Chelsea — also under new management with Antonio Conte — stormed to the title, Mourinho lifted the Carabao Cup and Europa League. It remains United's most successful post-Ferguson season in terms of silverware. Mourinho's claim that United's second-place finish in 2017/18 behind City's centurions was among the best of his career felt faintly ridiculous. Their efforts that season have aged pretty well but cracks were already beginning to appear, most notably between the manager and his flagship signing Paul Pogba. By the time Mourinho was sacked after a December 2018 defeat at Liverpool, United were a struggling mid-table rabble. Jose Mourinho Man United record : P 144 W84 D31 L29 (58.3% win percentage) Ole Gunnar Solskjaer Solskjaer's talking of "playing with a smile on your face", "the boss" and "Man United DNA" all felt faintly unserious amid the Klopp-Guardiola era, but it's hard to conclusively argue against the view that he remains United's best manager since his old mentor Ferguson. Perhaps he lacked a wider tactical vision regarding how to dominate games, but there really is something to be said for making things feel good and fun, especially after the late Mourinho toxicity. An improbable Champions League last-16 comeback at Paris Saint-Germain all but sealed Solskjaer's transition from interim to permanent boss. In 2020/21, they finished second to City — his record in derbies against Guardiola, especially away from home, was excellent — and agonisingly lost the Europa League final on penalties to Villarreal. Solskjaer had an energetic, hard-working side and foundations to build on. Naturally, United brought back Cristiano Ronaldo , completely torpedoed the manager's system and he was out of a job after a November 2021 hammering at Watford. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer Man United record : Pl68 W92 D35 L41 (54.76% win percentage) Ralf Rangnick United appointing the high priest of gegenpressing to oversee an attack led by Ronaldo and an increasingly disinterested squad to see them through to the end of the season is the sort of decision a club makes when no one really knows what they're doing. Rangnick followed in the footsteps of his predecessors by getting hammered at City and Liverpool. Once it started to become clear that his move into a vaguely-defined consultancy role was unlikely to materialise, Rangnick repeatedly cut loose in public, telling press conferences that the squad was ill-suited to modern tactical demands and needed an overhaul. It was difficult to argue with many of his conclusions , but this felt an awful lot more like self-preservation than leadership. Ralf Rangnick Man United record : P29 W11 D9 L9 (39.93% win percentage) Erik ten Hag The first two-thirds of Ten Hag's maiden season in charge were an unquestionable success. The Dutchman put United in the mix near the top of the table, jettisoned a malcontent Ronaldo, beat City at Old Trafford and won the Carabao Cup. Then they went to Anfield. Hello, old friend. Liverpool, who actually finished below United in the table in 2022/23, ran out 7-0 winners. Things were never the same after that. The 2023/24 campaign — an eighth-place finish and a group-stage exit in the Champions League — was roundly awful until United avenged their 2023 FA Cup final defeat to City and made it two trop

item.title: Dortmund still without Karetsas for Cup match against Bremen
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Borussia Dortmund's Konstantinos Karetsas pictured during the Club friendly soccer Match between Borussia Dortmund and AS Roma. (is associated with: «Dortmund still without Karetsas for Cup match against Bremen») Bernd Thissen/dpa Borussia Dortmund will still be without newcomer Konstantinos Karetsas for the German Cup match against Werder Bremen on Tuesday. "He's still not ready to play. He just started to run. He's positive, I'm happy about that. For the next games, we will see," coach Niko Kovac said in a news conference on Monday. Karetsas missed the Champions League match against Sabah last Tuesday and the Bundesliga clash against Eintracht Frankfurt last Saturday due to ligament injury in his foot. Dortmund will hope to have him available for the league table-topper against Bayern Munich on Saturday. Ahead of the clash against Bremen, Kovac recalled their most recent meeting earlier this month, which ended in a 2-2 draw, and warned his players of in-form striker Niclas Füllkrug. "He's the one who stands out with his goals. A very good player, otherwise he wouldn't have become a national team player. He's not easy to stop. He's very dominant on set pieces and is the one everyone looks for," Kovac said. Füllkrug, a former Dortmund player, returned to Bremen on loan from West Ham this season after his departure in 2023. He's been having an impressive run so far, with nine goals in eight matches across all competitions.

item.title: What exactly happened on that 4th and 1?
item.description: COLUMBIA, SOUTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 24: Sam Pendleton #56 of the Tennessee Volunteers prepares to snap the ball during the first half of a football game against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Williams-Brice Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Columbia, South Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images With 3:38 to play in the fourth quarter on Saturday, Tennessee was faced with a 4th and 1 situation at the South Carolina 38 yard line. The game hanging in the balance, it would have been about a 55-yard attempt for Cooper Ranvier, who has a career long of 51. He’s 2-6 from 50+ in his career. Tennessee had battled back. They really had dominated since South Carolina’s 14-0 burst out of the opening gates. Josh Heupel had a chance to put this one on ice and opted to go for it, even with star running back DeSean Bishop sidelined with a sudden injury. The play could not have gone worse. Tennessee quarterback George MacIntyre didn’t hand the ball off to DaSaahn Brame as it appeared it was intended. Javin Gordon was clearly never expecting the ball. It’s not exactly clear what MacIntyre was trying to do, but the end result was a loss of two yards and a turnover on downs that set up South Carolina for the tie and eventual win. It’s worth wondering how Bishop’s absence from the play changed things. Busted play by Tennessee on 4th down pic.twitter.com/GZ7BfzX3iA — gmannVOLS (@gmannVOLS) October 24, 2026 “Yeah, just missteps by George on that one,” Heupel said after the game of the play. The formation was one that Tennessee had used quite a bit throughout the afternoon with great success. It’s a fairly new look for the offense, and obviously with MacIntyre making just his third career start, it was new to him too. “Yeah, just simple miscommunication — a formation we’ve been running all game,” MacIntyre said after the loss. “Just got to be more locked into the details of the different plays and that big jumbo formation. “There’s a lot of moving parts of the play with kills and checks and what fronts they’re going to run. But, yeah, it would have been similar to DaSaahn’s touchdown in the first half.” LaNorris Sellers would go down and score quickly to tie the game at 24-24. MacIntyre would fumble shortly after, giving South Carolina the ball and a shot at the game-winning field goal. Frustrating penalties aside, this was a true choke job late from Tennessee. Through the slow start and all of the touchdowns called back, the Volunteers were in complete control of this one — until they weren’t. Tennessee has a week to think about this one before taking on No. 9 Kentucky in Knoxville on November 7th.
item.content:encoded: COLUMBIA, SOUTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 24: Sam Pendleton #56 of the Tennessee Volunteers prepares to snap the ball during the first half of a football game against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Williams-Brice Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Columbia, South Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images With 3:38 to play in the fourth quarter on Saturday, Tennessee was faced with a 4th and 1 situation at the South Carolina 38 yard line. The game hanging in the balance, it would have been about a 55-yard attempt for Cooper Ranvier, who has a career long of 51. He’s 2-6 from 50+ in his career. Tennessee had battled back. They really had dominated since South Carolina’s 14-0 burst out of the opening gates. Josh Heupel had a chance to put this one on ice and opted to go for it, even with star running back DeSean Bishop sidelined with a sudden injury. The play could not have gone worse. Tennessee quarterback George MacIntyre didn’t hand the ball off to DaSaahn Brame as it appeared it was intended. Javin Gordon was clearly never expecting the ball. It’s not exactly clear what MacIntyre was trying to do, but the end result was a loss of two yards and a turnover on downs that set up South Carolina for the tie and eventual win. It’s worth wondering how Bishop’s absence from the play changed things. Busted play by Tennessee on 4th down pic.twitter.com/GZ7BfzX3iA — gmannVOLS (@gmannVOLS) October 24, 2026 “Yeah, just missteps by George on that one,” Heupel said after the game of the play. The formation was one that Tennessee had used quite a bit throughout the afternoon with great success. It’s a fairly new look for the offense, and obviously with MacIntyre making just his third career start, it was new to him too. “Yeah, just simple miscommunication — a formation we’ve been running all game,” MacIntyre said after the loss. “Just got to be more locked into the details of the different plays and that big jumbo formation. “There’s a lot of moving parts of the play with kills and checks and what fronts they’re going to run. But, yeah, it would have been similar to DaSaahn’s touchdown in the first half.” LaNorris Sellers would go down and score quickly to tie the game at 24-24. MacIntyre would fumble shortly after, giving South Carolina the ball and a shot at the game-winning field goal. Frustrating penalties aside, this was a true choke job late from Tennessee. Through the slow start and all of the touchdowns called back, the Volunteers were in complete control of this one — until they weren’t. Tennessee has a week to think about this one before taking on No. 9 Kentucky in Knoxville on November 7th.

item.title: Guardians News: Three Positives From the Final Week of the Season
item.description: I know what you’re thinking. “How can I be positive when the season is over? I have to watch two other teams play in the World Series when it should be us instead.” And yes, I’ve been feeling the same way over the last week. However hard it has been, though, I am extremely proud of what this team accomplished this year and super happy to have been a part of it. Hard Fought Final Game While the Tampa Bay Rays took an early lead in Monday’s game six, the Guardians did all they could to fight back. Nathaniel Lowe got the scoring started in the sixth inning with an RBI single. While Junior Caminero extended the Rays’ lead in the bottom of the seventh inning, the Guardians did all they could to come back in the eighth. While pitcher Tyler Wells loaded the bases, he was replaced by Ian Seymour who walked in a run and hit Angel Martínez to make it 5-3. That was where the magic ended, however, as Yandy Díaz tacked on two more with a home run in the bottom of the inning. While the Guardians’ season came to an end, this was the farthest they’ve made it in the past decade. Bibee Wins Fielding Bible Award For the second time in his career, Tanner Bibee has won the Fielding Bibe Award. This is awarded to one player at each position for being the best defender. Bibee previously won this award in 2024 and remains the only Guardians pitcher to have won it. With 11 putouts, 18 assists, and a .906 fielding percentage, this was the second-best defensive year of Bibee’s career. As you can imagine, it is second to his 2024 Fielding Bible Award-winning season. Vogt Confirms Return in 2027 As the season came to a close on Monday, rumors immediately started flowing. Chief among those were rumors of manager Stephen Vogt leaving the team. With the announcement of the departure of Seattle Mariners manager Dan Wilson, many thought that Vogt would want to try for the job. His family lives in Washington, and he served as the Mariners’ bullpen coach in 2023 after retiring as a player. However, he made it clear that he will be back in Cleveland in 2027. “I’ll be in Cleveland,” he said. “I’m here. I’m coming back.”

item.title: 49ers’ George Kittle knows it’s no secret why San Francisco took first L against Falcons
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images 49ers’ George Kittle knows it’s no secret why San Francisco took first L against Falcons appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . George Kittle believes the San Francisco 49ers have nobody to blame but themselves after suffering their first loss of 2026. San Francisco fell 29-20 to the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, with Brock Purdy also refusing to make excuses. The defeat ended San Francisco’s perfect 6-0 start, exposing costly mistakes that overshadowed another promising offensive performance. Speaking after the game, Kittle identified four turnovers as the biggest reason the 49ers failed to remain undefeated. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Four turnovers, hard to win football games,” Kittle said in a postgame video shared by Greg Auman. The veteran tight end explained that San Francisco’s frustration began before halftime, particularly after wasting opportunities near Atlanta’s end zone. “Thought at halftime, I think we were just disappointed in ourselves for having turnovers in the red zone,” Kittle said. San Francisco initially built a 14-3 advantage before Atlanta fought back. The Falcons eventually converted the 49ers’ four turnovers into 13 points. Purdy threw two interceptions, while rookie running back Kaelon Black lost a fumble. Kittle also fumbled during San Francisco’s final possession, ending another potential scoring opportunity. Atlanta safety Jessie Bates III contributed an interception and forced Kittle’s late fumble. His game-changing defensive performance helped the Falcons secure their third victory. Kittle acknowledged that San Francisco still had opportunities to win despite those mistakes. “Still had a chance at the end. It’s just not good football,” he admitted. The 49ers enter their Week 8 bye at 6-1, giving them time to address their turnover problems. Despite the disappointing result, Kittle believes San Francisco remains capable of competing, provided the team eliminates costly mistakes in crucial moments. Related: 49ers’ Brock Purdy makes zero injury excuses after turnover fest ruins undefeated season Related: 49ers’ Brock Purdy explains brutal blunder that cost San Francisco during Falcons upset

item.title: 5 players Yankees could consider trading for during 2026-27 offseason
item.description: The Yankees need to make some changes to the roster, and the free agent market may not provide what GM Brian Cashman needs. Cashman may have to dive into the trade market to find a third baseman, second baseman and other pieces to try to get the 2027 Yankees to the World Series. It's been a while since Cashman made a substantial offseason trade, but the longtime exec usually surprises the baseball world, like he did when he picked up Juan Soto from the Padres ahead of the 2024 season. With Hal Steinbrenner putting a heavy emphasis on the team's offensive woes this past season, Cashman may need to wade into the trade waters to do it. He does have a surplus of major league ready starters and former prospects that can entice a team or two, but which players should he target? Here's a list of five players the Yankees could consider in a trade this offseason... Isaac Paredes Paredes is one of the more underrated players in baseball, but Cashman should really consider bringing the 27-year-old in this offseason. Houston has a club option to retain Paredes for just $13.35 million, which they certainly will, but that makes him all the more affordable as he enters the final year of his deal. And while the Astros won the AL West, they should consider moving the infielder when they can maximize his value, especially with what the Yankees can offer. The Yankees have starting pitching to deal in Will Warren, Ryan Weathers, or Clarke Schmidt , and can potentially package Carlos Lagrange in a deal. Paredes slashed .262/.360/.447 with an OPS of .807 to go along with his 25 home runs on an objectively bad Astros team. He was an All-Star in 2025, but had a better year in 2026, posting career highs in batting average, OBP and games played (155). Paredes' defense is below average, though. He had a -3 OAA at second base in 2026, while being a -4 in 2025 and a -2 in 2024. Paredes is young enough to be coached up to play the position better in 2027, so there is potential upside if the Yankees could pry him away from Houston. Zach McKinstry Another infield option is McKinstry, who doesn't have the offensive ceiling that Paredes has but gives manager Aaron Boone a ton of versatility. McKinstry has started at third base (four), shortstop (19), second base (28) and in all three outfield positions, with 49 starts in right field. If there's a downside, McKinstry is a left-handed bat, making him redundant at third base, and potentially second base if Luis Garcia Jr. becomes an option at the position. (It would give the Yankees the option to trade Garcia to another team). But it's hard to overlook his ability to play multiple positions and is just one year removed from being an All-Star and a Silver Slugger. While he slashed just .199/.288/.294 with an OPS of .582 -- to go with just four home runs -- his All-Star season saw him slash .259/.333/.438 with an OPS of .771 and 12 home runs, all career highs. item.content:encoded: The Yankees need to make some changes to the roster, and the free agent market may not provide what GM Brian Cashman needs. Cashman may have to dive into the trade market to find a third baseman, second baseman and other pieces to try to get the 2027 Yankees to the World Series. It's been a while since Cashman made a substantial offseason trade, but the longtime exec usually surprises the baseball world, like he did when he picked up Juan Soto from the Padres ahead of the 2024 season. The Yankees have starting pitching to deal in Will Warren, Ryan Weathers, or Clarke Schmidt , and can potentially package Carlos Lagrange in a deal. Paredes slashed .262/.360/.447 with an OPS of .807 to go along with his 25 home runs on an objectively bad Astros team. He was an All-Star in 2025, but had a better year in 2026, posting career highs in batting average, OBP and games played (155). Paredes' defense is below average, though. He had a -3 OAA at second base in 2026, while being a -4 in 2025 and a -2 in 2024. Paredes is young enough to be coached up to play the position better in 2027, so there is potential upside if the Yankees could pry him away from Houston. Zach McKinstry Another infield option is McKinstry, who doesn't have the offensive ceiling that Paredes has but gives manager Aaron Boone a ton of versatility. McKinstry has started at third base (four), shortstop (19), second base (28) and in all three outfield positions, with 49 starts in right field. If there's a downside, McKinstry is a left-handed bat, making him redundant at third base, and potentially second base if Luis Garcia Jr. becomes an option at the position. (It would give the Yankees the option to trade Garcia to another team). But it's hard to overlook his ability to play multiple positions and is just one year removed from being an All-Star and a Silver Slugger. While he slashed just .199/.288/.294 with an OPS of .582 -- to go with just four home runs -- his All-Star season saw him slash .259/.333/.438 with an OPS of .771 and 12 home runs, all career highs. Could McKinstry bounce back and be a good platoon option? It may not take much to get him from the Tigers, especially if the Yankees can dangle Jasson Dominguez, a young outfield prospect. Jul 21, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Washington Nationals shortstop CJ Abrams (5) rounds the bases on a two run home run in the first inning against the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field. / Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images CJ Abrams The Yankees reportedly checked in on Abrams at this past deadline, and they should ask the Nationals for his services again. Abrams is coming off a career year where he slashed .261/.336/.497 with an OPS of .833, to go with 33 home runs and 106 RBI. But this deal would only work if Abrams plays second base, which Washington began to transition him to at the end of 2026. He finished playing 14 games (12 starts) at the position and made every play hit to him. He would be Jazz Chisholm Jr. 's replacement, and while not as good defensively, he was better offensively and hit better against left-handers. He batted .240 with eight home runs and 63 strikeouts in 192 ABs facing southpaws. It's better than Chisholm's .218, five home runs and 56 strikeouts in 147 ABs, but would continue to make the Yankees lineup susceptible to southpaws. Abrams is still an intriguing option, especially since it looks as if the marriage between the Nats and the infielder is heading toward a divorce. Royce Lewis Another intriguing name. Lewis, a former No. 1 pick, has seen a lot of ups and downs with the Twins, and that continued this past season. Lewis was moved to first base, off of third, to improve the overall defense of the team, and that may have affected him at the plate. He hit .227 with 15 homers, 57 RBI, 16 stolen bases and a .667 OPS in 125 games, but he struggled so much at the start of the 2026 campaign that Minnesota demoted Lewis. To Lewis' credit, he bounced back, batting .280 with 28 extra-base hits and an .842 OPS in his first 59 games following his call-up. But he hit .187 over his last 35 games with just six extra-base hits and a .468 OPS. But it wasn't that long ago (2023 to be exact) that he batted .309 with 15 home runs in just 58 games. With experience at third and first base, and being a right-handed bat to complement Ryan McMahon and Ben Rice /Garcia Jr., the Yankees should see whether he's available. He has two more years of team control and could be a viable "buy-low" option for Cashman, to see whether they can get the 27-year-old back on track. Twins could use starting pitching and outfield help, both the Yankees can provide. Nolan Arenado What is this, 2024? Feels like forever ago that the Yankees were connected to Arenado. Of course, New York went with internal options and eventually McMahon to play the hot corner the last couple of years, but the perennial All-Star could be available again. The Yankees need a right-handed third baseman to pair with McMahon, and while Arenado isn't the Gold Glover at the position he once was, he's still very good. The last two seasons, he had a 2 OAA, the lowest of his career, but is still in the top 79th percentile, according to Baseball Savant. But the biggest development in a potential pursuit of Arenado is that his offense has rebounded. In 152 games, he slashed .255/.331/.475, a big jump from his .237/.289/.377 in 2025. His .806 OPS and 30(!) home runs are Arenado's highest since 2022. Should the Yankees expect the same production? No, but he's an upgrade over McMahon. And with Arenado in the final year of his contract, the Diamondbacks could look to sell high on the veteran and look to retool for another crack at the postseason.

item.title: Kovac updates on Karetsas and warns of Füllkrug threat ahead of Werder clash
item.description: Kovac updates on Karetsas and warns of Füllkrug threat ahead of Werder clash Having returned to winning ways with victories over Sabah FC (2-1) and Eintracht Frankfurt (1-0), Borussia Dortmund will look to extend their run when they face Werder Bremen in the second round of the DFB-Pokal on Tuesday. As BVB coach Niko Kovac confirmed on Monday, youngster Konstantinos Karetsas remains sidelined with the ligament injury he suffered during a 0-0 draw with 1. FC Union Berlin just over a week ago. “He’s not ready to play yet. I’ve just seen him. He’s at the very beginning of being able to walk in a straight line. He’s positive, which makes me happy. We’ll obviously see how things develop for the next few games,” Kovac said. Two and a half weeks on from Dortmund’s 2-2 draw with Werder Bremen in the Bundesliga, Kovac warned his side about former BVB forward Niclas Füllkrug, who scored a late equaliser in that encounter. “He’s the one who stands out because of his goals. He’s a very good player – otherwise, he wouldn’t have become an international. He’s not easy to keep quiet. He’s very dominant at set pieces, and he’s the player everyone looks for,” Kovac said of Füllkrug, who currently leads the Bundesliga scoring charts with eight goals. Dortmund last reached the DFB-Pokal final in May 2021 and will be hoping to return to Berlin this season. However, Kovac underlines that it's way too early to look that far ahead. “We’re playing at home, which is certainly an advantage. We can’t start thinking about Berlin just yet,” Kovac said. “Tomorrow is the next step. First, we have to take this one before we’re allowed to take the next.”

item.title: Giants QB JJ McCarthy’s wife drops ‘love’-filled message after Texans win
item.description: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images. Giants QB JJ McCarthy’s wife drops ‘love’-filled message after Texans win appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After her husband led the New York Giants ’ win over the Houston Texans, JJ McCarthy ’s wife Katya posted a message of “love” on Instagram. Katya McCarthy took to her Instagram Stories to celebrate her husband’s first win in his first start with Big Blue, writing, “God, I love you [heart on fire emoji]. So deserving,” over a video of him celebrating Devin Singletary’s game-winning overtime touchdown. JJ and Katya McCarthy are high school sweethearts. He proposed to her in 2024 after winning the national championship with Michigan. Their first child was born in September 2025. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) JJ McCarthy’s first start as Giants’ QB vs. Texans Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Just under a month after being traded to the Giants, McCarthy started his first game of the year, replacing Jameis Winston . He only started 10 games in his two years with the Minnesota Vikings, who drafted him in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft. McCarthy completed 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards. The Giants rushed for four touchdowns. Cam Skattebo, Devin Singletary, Tyrone Tracy Jr., and Winston all scored one. McCarthy only rushed for one yard. Malik Nabers and Malachi Fields benefited the most from McCarthy starting. The former logged 111 yards on seven catches, while the latter had 83 yards on four catches. The Giants’ defense held CJ Stroud in check. He only averaged 5.5 yards per attempt, passing for 153 yards on 28 pass attempts. He did throw two touchdowns, though. Now, the Giants await the result of the Week 7 Monday Night Football game. Their divisional rivals, the Dallas Cowboys and the Philadelphia 76ers, will play on Monday Night Football. The loser of the game will drop to 2-5. The Giants lead the NFC East at 4-2-1. Philadelphia and Dallas are tied in second place at 2-4, while the Washington Commanders are right behind them at 1-4-1. The Giants will next play the Philadelphia Eagles coming out of their bye in Week 9. Related: Giants’ JJ McCarthy gets his NY locker room moment after Texans win Related: Giants’ Cam Skattebo calls out NFL double standard after ridiculous penalty during Texans game

item.title: TICKET INFORMATION
item.description: TICKET INFORMATION Manchester City will play Napoli at home in the League Phase of the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday 24th November, kick off 8pm. Following the draw in August, the Club are implementing additional ticketing measures to reduce the risk of away fans in home areas of the stadium. When fans purchase more than one ticket, the named ticket holder (the purchaser) must be one of those in attendance and is responsible for the behaviour of their guests. Any ticket holder found to have played a role in allowing an away fan into the home sections will be subject to a stadium ban in line with the Club’s sanctions and bans policy. Cup Scheme payments will be taken on Monday 2 November. UEFA Cup Scheme Members do not need to purchase their ticket.

item.title: Plenty of blame to go around for Packers in loss to Lions
item.description: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-OCTOBER 25: Head coach Matt LaFleur of the Green Bay Packers talks to referee Alex Moore #49 during the second half of an NFL football game between the Green Bay Packers and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, October 25, 2026 (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Blame the referees. Blame the kicker. Blame the drops. The Green Bay Packers can find a way to put blame on every single person who went out between the lines at Ford Field for their 20-17 loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday. That includes both teams and the cohort of referees, all of whom contributed to yet another excruciating, frustrating loss. The refs put the Packers in terrible positions time and time again with bad, inconsistent officiating, and yet the team still had plenty of opportunities to win the game. They let those chances slip through their fingers — literally, in many cases — and now they sit at 4-3, in fourth place in the NFC North division, and on the cusp of undoing all of the good that had come from their recent three-game winning streak. Going 5-for-15 on third downs isn’t good enough. Jordan Love can’t will this team to a 50 percent conversion rate every game, particularly not when the team can’t get out of its own way on first and second down and when his receivers can’t hold on to the football. Going 1-for-4 in the red zone, thanks in large part to a pair of missed chip shot field goals (one of which was blocked), isn’t good enough. And so, here we are, seven weeks into the season and still holding more questions than answers about this team. This is not intended as criticism, but it’s notable that Mike Spofford takes the team to task rather than the officials. Packers rip officiating after roughing penalties prove costly in loss | ESPN The players, meanwhile — especially on defense — weren’t pulling any punches in the locker room, however. Xavier McKinney was the most outspoken, and he’ll surely get fined for his comments, but at this point someone has to call out the league’s embarrassing officating. Matt LaFleur Nailed It, But Will Anything Change for Packers After Loss to Lions? | SI.com The comment referred to in the headline here is LaFleur saying “We’ve got to grow up fast.” It’s tough to argue that the Packers were truly that immature in this game, though, when you have two roughing the passer calls that are questionable at best and another personal foul for tackling a player despite the whistle never blowing. Josh Jacobs apologizes to team after crucial drop in loss to Lions | Packers Wire Jacobs’ drop led directly to a field goal attempt that got blocked (but might have been missed anyway). Green Bay Packers rookie kicker Trey Smack takes blame for missed field goals | Packersnews.com ($) Somehow, Smack doesn’t have t

item.title: Al Nassr ready to offer lucrative renewal to star forward obsessed about Barcelona return
item.description: Al Nassr ready to offer lucrative renewal to star forward obsessed about Barcelona return The future of Joao Felix has become a key talking point in Saudi Arabia, especially after his superb performances in the league. Since joining Al Nassr, Felix has been on fire, racking up 31 goals and 24 assists in 59 competitive matches. He has emerged as one of the best players in the entire Saudi league. But Felix’s contract expires in the summer of 2027, which has led to question marks over his future. Felix obssessed about Barcelona return With his contract at Al Nassr expiring soon, Felix appears to be harbouring thoughts of a potential return to European football. Felix has been on fire in Saudi Arabia. (Photo by Abdullah Ahmed/Getty Images) According to SPORT , the Portuguese international is obsessed about the idea of returning to Barcelona, a club he played for briefly on a loan deal. Felix enjoyed his brief spell under Xavi Hernandez and harbours a great deal of love for the Blaugrana . Much like Joao Cancelo, the attacker is now keen on ensuring a return to Catalonia . Felix has made his desire public as well, openly stating his love for the club. So if he does indeed end up returning to Europe, Camp Nou would be his preferred choice. Al Nassr have the upper hand Unfortunately, though, Felix’s future is not in his own hands at the moment. The dream to return to Barcelona looks distant for Felix. (Photo by Abdullah Ahmed/Getty Images) This is thanks to a special clause that the player had agreed to at the time of signing for Al Nassr. The claude effectively gives the Saudi Arabian outfit the liberty to extend his contract for two more years without needing Felix’s signature. The two-year deal will see Felix’s contract being extended until 2029 and comes with a sizable increase in his current salary of €10 million annually. In light of his brilliant performances, the Saudi club are planning to add further financial incentive, in an attempt to coax the player to remain at Al Nassr. The only condition in the clause is that it will have to be activated by May 2027, which is unlikely to be a problem for the club.

item.title: 3 NFL teams that should be worried after Week 7
item.description: NFL Week 7 is almost in the books, pending Monday Night’s NFC East showdown, and this Sunday shone a new light on a few teams we think should be worried as we head into Week 8. The San Francisco 49ers suffered their first loss, and while we are certainly concerned due to the rash of injuries they have suffered lately, we are going to give them a pass as they will now get a week off to lick their wounds with their bye. Three other teams really kicked the worry meter into overdrive this weekend that we’d like to discuss. Let’s jump in and look at which teams might be in big trouble after week 7. MORE: Boomer Esiason suggests blockbuster NFL trade between Cowboys & Chargers The Carolina Panthers Oct 18, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young (9) throws a pass against the Philadelphia Eagles during the second half at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images The Panthers were apparently a bunch of paper tigers through 6 weeks, leading their division with a 3-2 record and a chance to put Baker Mayfield and the Bucs down for the count. Saying that they weren’t able to get the job done at home might be the understatement of the year, as they were completely embarrassed by the Buccaneers. The Carolina defense was shredded by the Tampa running game as Mayfield was able to ease his wounded thumb back into action by merely handing the ball off 48 times on the day while attempting just 11 passes. The Panthers were outclassed on both sides of the ball and now drop to 3-3. While they still are in 1st place in the division, it’s pretty clear they aren’t quite as head and shoulders above the crowd as we had previously thought. They don’t have much time to dwell on this defeat as they now have to travel to Lambeau Field to take on the Packers this Thursday night. The Houston Texans Houston Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Losing at home as the day’s biggest favorite is about as bad as it gets. The Texans gave fans some hope with two straight wins after a horrendous 0-4 start. That hope has turned to dread as the Texans now sit in the standings among teams like the Colts and Titans. There is still enough season left to right the ship and give the Jaguars a run for their money, but not if this defense is going to get pushed around as they did on Sunday by the Giants. Their inability to run the ball and their trouble stopping the run will make this a long season in Houston. Next week they get a reprieve from the schedule gods and will take the week off to try and figure things out. They face the Chargers in week 9, so they still have a chance to get back into the AFC South race, but their margin for error is gone. MORE: Aaron Rodgers moves past Peyton Manning with historic NFL moment in Paris The New York Jets New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn hypes up his defense during the first half of the NFL game at Ford Field in Detroit, Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026.

Aaron Glenn looks overwhelmed at times on the sidelines as he tries to juggle calling the defense and trying to be the head coach. He’s not very good as a defensive coordinator, and he may be the worst head coach the Jets have ever had. Yes, we know that Todd Bowles and Adam Gase coached this team. This season is basically lost, and this team will be flush with draft picks next Spring. They need to figure out who will lead the charge next season before they do anything else. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Cole Palmer available for Chelsea against Manchester United despite Tottenham red card
item.description: Cole Palmer available for Chelsea against Manchester United despite Tottenham red card Cole Palmer will be available to face Manchester United on Saturday despite his dismissal during Chelsea’s defeat to Tottenham Hotspur. United head to Chelsea amid an eight-match winless run United’s trip to Stamford Bridge comes at the end of a miserable October. A 4-1 Champions League defeat away to Como was followed by Sunday’s 3-0 loss to Bournemouth at Old Trafford, extending their winless run to eight matches in all competitions. The Red Devils sit 16th in the Premier League, one point above the relegation zone, after winning only two of their opening eight league games. They have also been eliminated from the Carabao Cup and lost their first three Champions League fixtures. Head coach Michael Carrick’s position is now under severe pressure. United’s hierarchy began crisis talks after the Bournemouth defeat, with another managerial change under consideration . There is also uncertainty surrounding captain Bruno Fernandes , who was left on the bench throughout the Bournemouth loss after publicly questioning United’s tactics following the defeat in Como. Chelsea have problems of their own after losing 2-0 at home to Tottenham on Saturday. Palmer was dismissed after receiving two yellow cards, with the second coming after he stood on Conor Gallagher’s ankle. Palmer will serve his suspension at Anfield Palmer’s ban carries across domestic competitions, meaning Chelsea’s Carabao Cup fourth-round tie away to Liverpool on Wednesday counts as the one match he must miss. He will therefore be eligible when United visit Stamford Bridge three days later. The dismissal was the first of Palmer’s senior career. Chelsea’s No. 10 addressed his conduct after the match and apologised to the club’s supporters. Palmer wrote: “Not good enough by me. Live n learn. Apologies. On to the next.” Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso said: “I need to check the action to talk with Cole, but it is one to learn for the future for sure” ( via Sports Illustrated ). The Blues will have to negotiate the trip to Anfield without him before restoring him to their options against United. Palmer will almost certainly be standing on the Stamford Bridge pitch at 12.30pm on Saturday. Whether Bruno Fernandes and Michael Carrick will also be taking part in the game remains to be seen. Final Thoughts Palmer will miss Chelsea’s Carabao Cup tie against Liverpool through suspension. It mean the England man will be available to face United at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

item.title: Cody Gakpo issues rallying cry to Liverpool squad ahead of massive Chelsea & Arsenal clashes
item.description: Liverpool FC Training Session And Press Conference - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 - Getty Images Sport Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo has called on his teammates to maintain their relentless momentum as the club enters a defining period of the season. Following a convincing victory over Brighton, the Dutchman believes the squad is finding another gear just in time for high-stakes encounters at Anfield. Maintaining the winning momentum Liverpool continued their impressive run of form on Sunday, securing a fourth consecutive victory across all competitions with a disciplined 2-0 win over Brighton & Hove Albion at Anfield. The result has solidified the positive atmosphere around the club, but Gakpo is already looking toward the significant challenges that lie immediately ahead. With a Carabao Cup tie against Chelsea followed by a Premier League showdown with Arsenal, the forward is demanding total focus from the dressing room. Speaking after the win against the Seagulls, Gakpo reflected on the development of the team under the current regime. "I think the most positive thing is that we feel that we are growing and obviously where it will end we don’t know, but we’re going to see in the end," said the Netherlands international on the club's official website . The forward highlighted that this progress feels sustainable rather than temporary. "But we are going and sometimes you don’t have this feeling, sometimes you have the feeling that we’re just playing well because of today’s game. But we have a feeling that we are growing every game and things are looking better and better. Obviously we’re going to play some games which are not going to be that good, but I think if we keep the feeling and keep this mentality to go all in then it looks good," he added. The power of the Anfield crowd A major factor in Liverpool’s recent success has been their home form, and Gakpo is acutely aware of how much the supporters influence the outcome of big matches. As Chelsea and Arsenal prepare to visit Merseyside, the Dutchman is banking on the "twelfth man" to provide an edge. The atmosphere at Anfield remains one of the most intimidating in world football, and Gakpo believes the players' energy on the pitch directly feeds the crowd’s intensity. "Obviously it’s always a big help if we play at home and I think if we can put the energy like we put in now, I think we’re going to get massive help from the fans because they are always behind us," Gakpo explained when discussing the upcoming week. "But obviously when we play a little bit better, they’re even more behind us, so it’s amazing that they are there for us every time again, even when it’s stormy like today. It’s a big help and to play Chelsea at home and then obviously Arsenal at home is good if we get them behind us." But we have a feeling that we are growing every game and things are looking better and better. Obviously we’re going to play some games which are not going to be that good, but I think if we keep the feeling and keep this mentality to go all in then it looks good," he added. The power of the Anfield crowd A major factor in Liverpool’s recent success has been their home form, and Gakpo is acutely aware of how much the supporters influence the outcome of big matches. As Chelsea and Arsenal prepare to visit Merseyside, the Dutchman is banking on the "twelfth man" to provide an edge. "Obviously it’s always a big help if we play at home and I think if we can put the energy like we put in now, I think we’re going to get massive help from the fans because they are always behind us," Gakpo explained when discussing the upcoming week. "But obviously when we play a little bit better, they’re even more behind us, so it’s amazing that they are there for us every time again, even when it’s stormy like today. It’s a big help and to play Chelsea at home and then obviously Arsenal at home is good if we get them behind us." Breaking down a resilient Brighton The victory over Brighton was no small feat, as the visitors arrived at Anfield boasting an incredible defensive record and four straight wins. However, a ruthless four-minute spell in the first half changed the complexion of the game. A Pascal Gross own goal, followed by a clinical strike from Alexander Isak, ensured the three points stayed on Merseyside. Gakpo noted the importance of the result given the quality of the opposition they faced. "I think it is a very big day, obviously [against] a very good side. I think the last few games for them they were flying, scoring a lot of goals, they don’t really concede much. For us, obviously important to get the first home win in the league, and I’m very happy with it. It was a real team win. I think we showed a lot of bravery in defence, sometimes just taking a risk being one-v-one in the back, but I think we as the players, and obviously the staff also, trust us to be in those positions and in front as well," Gakpo noted. Aggression and clinical finishing The tactical approach against Brighton emphasized high pressure and a refusal to settle for a narrow lead. Gakpo pointed to the second goal as a prime example of the squad's desire to kill games off early. Even after the deadlock was broken through a slice of luck involving Florian Wirtz, the instruction from the touchline remained clear: do not stop attacking. This proactive mindset is exactly what the forward believes will be necessary against the London clubs. "If we feel like we have to go and try to create something, obviously sometimes it doesn’t work out, but we can just go and everybody [will] accept and try to make the best out of it," he stated.

item.title: Winnebago Lutheran soccer is two wins away from trip to state
item.description: FOND DU LAC – The Winnebago Lutheran boys soccer team is two wins away from a trip to state. Winnebago Lutheran is a No. 4 seed and started its postseason journey with a penalty shootout win over No. 13 Central Wisconsin Christian. Wyatt Smallish finished with two saves in the win. In the region championship against No. 5 Lodi, Winnebago Lutheran won 1-0 with a goal by Micah Toll. Smallish finished the game with three saves. More: Bauer runs for 4 touchdowns in Lourdes Academy win | Level 1 roundup More: Quandt caps Lourdes Academy career with second place medal at state Winnebago Lutheran is now onto the Division 4 sectional semifinals and will hit the road for a matchup against No. 1 Lake Country Lutheran. The game will be at 7 p.m., Thursday, Oct. 29 at Lake Country Lutheran. The winner will face No. 2 Lake Mills or No. 3 Wisconsin Heights/Barneveld on Saturday, Oct. 31 with the time and place to be determined. Lake Country Lutheran has dominated in its first two games with a 9-0 win over No. 16 Lomira and an 8-1 win over No. 8 East Troy. Winnebago Lutheran is looking to make it back to state for the first time since 2016. The state tournament will be held from Nov. 5 – Nov. 7 at Uihlein Soccer Park in Milwaukee. Contact or send game stats/info to Ben Schultz at BSchultz@usatodayco.com. Follow him on X, formerly known as Twitter, @benschultz52. This article originally appeared on Oshkosh Northwestern: Winnebago Lutheran soccer is two wins away from trip to state

item.title: Hogg 'over the moon' following win over Colchester
item.description: Chris Hogg was appointed Cobblers boss in May [Getty Images] Northampton Town manager Chris Hogg said he was "over the moon" with his side following their victory over fellow League Two strugglers Colchester United on Saturday. Matty Warhurst's first goal for the club at Sixfields gave the Cobblers the perfect platform after nine minutes and Sam Hoskins flicked in a second five minutes after half-time to seal a 2-0 victory . Northampton's much needed three points lifted the club out of the relegation zone and up to 19th in League Two, leapfrogging Colchester in the process. It was Town's second win in three matches, backing up their win at Grimsby although they did lose 1-0 to Tranmere three days later, in which Hogg believed they played well. "Some of the performance levels over the last couple of games has been closer to what we want and especially on Tuesday night [against Grimsby] when you don't get the result," Hogg told BBC Radio Northampton. "It's been a really positive week to build the belief – I'm absolutely delighted and over the moon for the players. "I thought you saw a team playing to win rather than playing not to lose, which is a big difference in the mindset. I'm saying it every day to the players, we have to stop playing football games not to lose. We have to play to win." Former AC Milan and Brazil striker Alexandre Pato was in attendance for Northampton's victory on Saturday [Getty Images] Hogg singled out striker Warhurst for praise. It was the 20-year-old's second league goal since his move from Manchester City's academy in the summer. "[I'm] delighted for Matty. He's got to keep growing and keep believing in himself," he said. "Some of his out of possession work was terrific - that was rewards for his efforts." Following the takeover by Sports Alpha Capital , the club's new director Alexandre Pato was also in attendance on Saturday for the game against Colchester - a club he was also close to investing in earlier this year. Hogg said he hoped the team's progress will have left an impression on the former AC Milan, Chelsea and Brazil forward who he added is becoming a lucky charm for his side. "As I've said to Pato, he can come again because he was at the Newport game and we managed to win that one at home and we won again [on Saturday]," Hogg added.
