item.title: Would a Brian Thomas Jr. Trade Make Sense for Steelers?
item.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. and Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Brandin Echols on Aug. 9, 2025. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Even after an impressive 5-2 start to the season, the Pittsburgh Steelers offense continues to have issues putting points on the board. Through seven weeks, the passing attack led by Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy ranks 27th in dropback EPA per play and 21st in success rate. Their rushing attack continues to be both efficient and explosive, but drives have stagnated too often in third-and-medium and red-zone situations. With two wide receivers, Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson , already on injured reserve, it begs the question: Should this be a team looking to trade for another playmaker? Steelers offensive rankings through week 7, pending MNF: EPA/play: 20th Success rate: 22nd Dropback EPA: 27th Dropback success rate: 25th Rushing EPA: 2nd Rushing success rate: 12th — Derrick (@Steelers_DB) October 26, 2026 One of the hottest names on the rumor mill is Brian Thomas Jr. , the Jaguars’ third-year wideout who has fallen down the pecking order in Liam Coen’s offense following the ascension of Parker Washington and the arrival of Jakobi Meyers. The LSU product didn’t play a single snap in the second half of Jacksonville’s loss to the Houston Texans last week, as the Jaguars instead unleashed Travis Hunter. Thomas is only a year and a half removed from an incredible rookie season in 2024, when he notched 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns. General manager Omar Khan has been trying to overhaul this position since taking over in 2023, so could Thomas be the potential missing piece? Speed is the name of his game. Thomas has the God-given ability to stack virtually any cornerback in the league on vertical routes with his explosiveness. The rare combination of burst off the ball and a blazing top gear makes him a legitimate lid lifter who can create space for his teammates underneath. He comes with a wealth of experience against press coverage and an understanding of how to win early in the rep by varying his releases or simply hitting the nitrous button immediately. This is a long-striding glider who eats up off-coverage cushion in an instant, striking the fear of God into opposing defensive backs by regularly forcing them to prematurely open their hips in an attempt to stay on top of him. pic.twitter.com/pXY9EoQKfo — Draft_247 (@Draft_247) October 26, 2026 What separates him from his peers in this receiver archetype is his surprising fluidity and lower-body flexibility, which allow him to snap defenders off at the break point. Thomas has flashed the ability to decelerate in ways that aren’t typical for players his size, crossing defenders’ faces and winning back leverage. Out-breaking routes have accounted for many of his best reps against man coverage. There are also glimpses of the craftsmanship you want to see at the NFL level, including being proactive with his hands throughout the route stem and display
item.content:encoded: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. and Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Brandin Echols on Aug. 9, 2025. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Even after an impressive 5-2 start to the season, the Pittsburgh Steelers offense continues to have issues putting points on the board. Through seven weeks, the passing attack led by Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy ranks 27th in dropback EPA per play and 21st in success rate. Their rushing attack continues to be both efficient and explosive, but drives have stagnated too often in third-and-medium and red-zone situations. With two wide receivers, Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson , already on injured reserve, it begs the question: Should this be a team looking to trade for another playmaker? Steelers offensive rankings through week 7, pending MNF: EPA/play: 20th Success rate: 22nd Dropback EPA: 27th Dropback success rate: 25th Rushing EPA: 2nd Rushing success rate: 12th — Derrick (@Steelers_DB) October 26, 2026 One of the hottest names on the rumor mill is Brian Thomas Jr. , the Jaguars’ third-year wideout who has fallen down the pecking order in Liam Coen’s offense following the ascension of Parker Washington and the arrival of Jakobi Meyers. The LSU product didn’t play a single snap in the second half of Jacksonville’s loss to the Houston Texans last week, as the Jaguars instead unleashed Travis Hunter. Thomas is only a year and a half removed from an incredible rookie season in 2024, when he notched 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns. General manager Omar Khan has been trying to overhaul this position since taking over in 2023, so could Thomas be the potential missing piece? Speed is the name of his game. Thomas has the God-given ability to stack virtually any cornerback in the league on vertical routes with his explosiveness. The rare combination of burst off the ball and a blazing top gear makes him a legitimate lid lifter who can create space for his teammates underneath. He comes with a wealth of experience against press coverage and an understanding of how to win early in the rep by varying his releases or simply hitting the nitrous button immediately. This is a long-striding glider who eats up off-coverage cushion in an instant, striking the fear of God into opposing defensive backs by regularly forcing them to prematurely open their hips in an attempt to stay on top of him. pic.twitter.com/pXY9EoQKfo — Draft_247 (@Draft_247) October 26, 2026 What separates him from his peers in this receiver archetype is his surprising fluidity and lower-body flexibility, which allow him to snap defenders off at the break point. Thomas has flashed the ability to decelerate in ways that aren’t typical for players his size, crossing defenders’ faces and winning back leverage. Out-breaking routes have accounted for many of his best reps against man coverage. There are also glimpses of the craftsmanship you want to see at the NFL level, including being proactive with his hands throughout the route stem and displaying late hands at the catch point. Those traits complement his tracking ability on over-the-shoulder throws downfield. There are a couple of massive weaknesses in Thomas’ game that have contributed to his being relegated to what has essentially become a sacrificial X role in the Jaguars’ offense this season. The biggest issue is that he’s struggled mightily against zone coverage and clearly has a long way to go in learning how to identify the defense’s soft spots. In 2025, there were numerous examples early in the season of him drifting on routes or pulling up prematurely in anticipation of contact. His execution on concepts that required him to run wrap-ins or deep digs was so catastrophic at times that it actively hurt the offense, even leading to turnovers. Jacksonville eventually eliminated those routes from his tree altogether. pic.twitter.com/n6Lwm8oYeA — Draft_247 (@Draft_247) October 26, 2026 He’s also had an inexplicably difficult time catching the football, failing to establish any semblance of chemistry or trust with Trevor Lawrence and often looking like a difficult target to throw to. The occasional focus drop is understandable, but some of his shortcomings are technique-related, with a frustrating mix of body catches and clapping at the football. For someone with such impressive measurables, Thomas doesn’t play particularly big at the catch point. His catch radius feels more theoretical than functional, as he’s struggled to make difficult grabs, particularly through contact in contested-catch situations. As he’s been continually phased out of the offense, his attention to detail in every phase has dwindled. For as much big-play potential as a DK Metcalf –Thomas duo would bring to the table, it’s a clunky fit given the similarities in their skill sets, not to mention the extreme volatility in both players’ games. Even though the tape and production have been disappointing recently, we’ve already seen Thomas’ talent on display at the professional level when he’s been healthy. But this type of swing for the fences would make more sense if the Steelers weren’t already heavily financially committed to Metcalf as their WR1 for years to come. By trading for Thomas now, the franchise would be betting that he’s capable of becoming a more well-rounded receiver than he’s shown to date. As is the case with any move, the cost matters a ton in this instance. No one is going to debate whether the former first-round pick could step into Wilson’s role in this offense and represent an upgrade. Fellow member of the 2024 draft class Marvin Harrison Jr., who has actually been less productive in the pros, just fetched a second-round pick a few weeks ago. So while Thomas’ stock has certainly fallen from where it once stood, the asking price doesn’t seem likely to be pennies on the dollar, particularly for a team looking to make a postseason run. Given his talent, there’s a realistic pathway for Thomas to turn his career around in the right ecosystem, but this doesn’t feel like a gamble worth taking from Pittsburgh’s perspective. Related Headlines DB’s Steelers Dudes & Duds: Queen Balls Out; Fautanu Struggles Steelers Daily News & Links: Aaron Rodgers Iced Out; Insane Jaylen Warren Stat Steelers Rival Suffers Yet Another Critical Injury Blow Read more at Steelers Now

item.title: Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum’s NBA drama is more entertaining than it should be
item.description: The referendum on the Boston Celtics’ bold decision to trade Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers this summer might last all season. Celtics win? Great trade! Celtics blow a 22-point lead while Jayson Tatum shoots 6-for-23 from the floor? Bad deal, “welcome to being the guy, JT.” Ultimately, NBA fans won’t know who “won” the Brown trade for a few years when the draft picks involved in the deal convey, unless the Sixers or Celtics win a championship before that happens. What’s already clear is there are still some hurt feelings for the players involved, and it’s leading to one of the most embarrassing war of words possible to start the new season. Tatum and Brown both commented on the beef that isn’t a beef on Saturday after an emoji on social media added more fuel to the fire. Here’s the timeline of events here: Jaylen Brown commented with the “cap” emoji — indicating someone is lying — when Tatum said he was surprised by the trade like everyone else in an Instagram video. Tatum gave a long response about Brown’s emoji after the Celtics beat the Knicks on Friday, saying there’s “no beef” between the two and said he’s disappointed it’s turned into a drama rather than appreciating what the two accomplished together. Brown responded to Tatum’s comment after the Sixers beat the Bucks on Saturday, and gave a couple memorable quotes. Let’s get into those below. Brown said he agreed with Tatum that there’s no beef. Then it got interesting. “Jayson comes from a wonderful family. We’ve accomplished some great things. He’s a hell of a basketball player. He’s got a great PR team. There’s no beef but there might be a little lamb chops and gravy. He should stay ready at all times.” Jaylen Brown on Jayson Tatum: “It’s no beef, but it might be little lamb chops and some gravy, you know what I mean? “He should stay ready at all times.” pic.twitter.com/1jkBUKguWr — Kris Rhim (@krisrhim1) October 25, 2026 Brown liked the “lamb chops and gravy” line so much he said it twice. He really thought that one was going to bang, but in the humble opinion of this nearly 40-year-old blogger, it reads as pretty cringeworthy. I wish someone would have followed up on the last line about Tatum needing to stay ready. What does that mean?! I actually really like that line from Brown, it’s so ridiculous and opaque that it hits that just right. That’s how you do it when you want to go viral. Here’s Tatum’s long quote on Brown’s emoji. Tatum said he’s too old for the drama, and that he and Brown need better communication. Watch his full response: . @RealBobManning asked Jayson Tatum about Jaylen Brown’s 🧢 comment, and he responded at length: pic.twitter.com/7vR7EbHi80 — Noa Dalzell 🏀 (@NoaDalzell) October 24, 2026 And here’s the screenshot of Brown’s cap emoji that started it all. Shout-out to Tatum for rocking the backwards red fitted cap in this video. I assume it’s a Cardinals hat for the St. Louis native, but that will always remind me of Fred Durst. Jayson Tatum on the Jaylen B

I actually really like that line from Brown, it’s so ridiculous and opaque that it hits that just right. That’s how you do it when you want to go viral. Here’s Tatum’s long quote on Brown’s emoji. Tatum said he’s too old for the drama, and that he and Brown need better communication. Watch his full response: . @RealBobManning asked Jayson Tatum about Jaylen Brown’s 🧢 comment, and he responded at length: pic.twitter.com/7vR7EbHi80 — Noa Dalzell 🏀 (@NoaDalzell) October 24, 2026 And here’s the screenshot of Brown’s cap emoji that started it all. Shout-out to Tatum for rocking the backwards red fitted cap in this video. I assume it’s a Cardinals hat for the St. Louis native, but that will always remind me of Fred Durst. Jayson Tatum on the Jaylen Brown trade in a recent interview: "I was just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world." Jaylen Brown in the comments: 🧢 pic.twitter.com/dia6lscJ2E — Underdog NBA (@UnderdogNBA) October 23, 2026 Here are some quick takes on the state of the Tatum-Brown relationship right now: I could be wrong about this, but … the Celtics *probably* told Tatum they were going to trade Brown just to make sure he didn’t have a bad reaction to it. In that sense, Brown likely isn’t wrong for using the cap emoji in response to Tatum saying he was totally caught off guard. Tatum’s response is far more mature, and this situation is clearly eating away at him a little bit. I’m sure he enjoyed his years with Brown. They won so many games, and that 2024 championship banner will hang forever. Brown seems to be using that trade and Tatum’s comments as motivation, which basically every athlete does. This should be a non-story, but that’s never going to happen because fans love drama. Brown is probably going to keep leaning in, and Tatum is probably going to continue to be stuck between a rock and a hard place. This is all very silly, but whatever. Get back to me in 2035 and we’ll see who really won the Jaylen Brown trade.

item.title: Official: Serie A hand two-game ban to Allegri, suspending him for Juventus return
item.description: Official: Serie A hand two-game ban to Allegri, suspending him for Juventus return Napoli head coach Massimiliano Allegri has been handed a two-game suspension by the Lega Serie A and will now be suspended for his upcoming matches against Monza and his former club Juventus. See the full list of suspensions after the eighth round of Serie A fixtures below. Allegri and Gaspar given two-match bans after Serie A Week 8 The eighth round of 2026-27 Serie A fixtures began on Friday night with Torino’s 3-2 victory over Monza and came to a close with Milan’s 2-0 win away against Udinese on Sunday night. Only one [layer was sent off during the weekend’s round of Serie A fixtures: Lecce’s Kiolonda Gaspar, who has earned a two-match suspension after being shown a straight red card for violent conduct, appearing to intentionally strike his opponent in the face with his arm. ITALY – OCTOBER 25: Kialonda Gaspar of US Lecce competes for the ball with Randal Kolo Muani of Juventus FC during the Serie A match between US Lecce and Juventus at Stadio Via del Mare on October 25, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Maurizio Lagana/Getty Images) No players have yet reached the five yellow card threshold to earn a one-match ban, although Frosinone’s Gabriele Bracaglia and Cagliari’s Alessandro Deiola are now on four each. The only other individual to earn a suspension this weekend was Napoli head coach Allegri, who was shown a red card for his protests after Leonardo Balerdi’s late equaliser in the 3-3 draw between the Partenopei and Roma on Saturday evening. NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 24: Massimiliano Allegri, SSC Napoli head coach, reacts to his expulsion during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and AS Roma at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 24, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Allegri took off his jacket and stormed off after being shown a red card, but returned a few moments later and needed to be held back by members of his coaching staff. His reaction has earned him a two-match ban, which means that he will not be permitted to sit in the dugout for Napoli’s next matches against Monza or away against Juventus next weekend.

item.title: The NFL’s Double Standards Debate Just Got More Complicated With Josh Allen
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has been putting on a show through the first quarter of the NFL season, making plays that few QBs can pull off. But for every highlight-reel moment, there have been a few head-scratching mistakes. Allen has racked up 15 total touchdowns this season, but he’s also coughed up the ball five times. His playmaking prowess has been a major reason behind Buffalo’s 4-1 start, but NFL fans believe the Bills superstar is getting off too easy for his costly turnovers. Why Josh Allen Gets Away With More Oct 18, 2026; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) throws in the first quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Brytus-Imagn Images The Buffalo Bills are off to a 4-1 start and are coming off a statement win over the Los Angeles Rams. But as the Bills keep stacking wins, Josh Allen’s all-too-familiar turnover problem continues to rear its ugly head. The bigger question, though, is whether Allen gets a different rulebook when it comes to criticism. While rival quarterbacks are branded overrated or have their games reduced to their rushing ability, the Bills superstar gets celebrated for his dual-threat brilliance and often gets a pass for his costly mistakes, with his supporting cast frequently entering the conversation. More so, the Bills also were against the Eagles’ famous tush-push and voted to ban it in the NFL, but in 2025, Josh Allen was one of the quarterbacks who used the tush-push the most. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ball Culture HD • Basketball • Hoops ™️ (@ballculturehd) To his credit, Allen has never shied away from owning his mistakes. The four-time MVP contender has often been his own harshest critic, taking accountability when things go sideways. But that hasn’t stopped the turnovers from becoming a recurring storyline. Take Buffalo’s Week 3 clash with the Los Angeles Chargers . Allen threw two interceptions and lost a fumble as the Bills coughed up the ball five times. Buffalo still escaped with a 24-16 win, but its defense had to step up to prevent those giveaways from turning into a late-game meltdown. The following week, Allen’s turnover bug bit again in a 29-26 loss to the New England Patriots . Trailing by three with 1:14 left on the clock, Allen escaped pressure and launched a deep ball toward Josh Palmer, only for safety Craig Woodson to come down with the game-sealing interception. Allen admitted afterward that he should have thrown the ball away. Of course, there’s another side to the story. Allen’s gunslinger mentality and off-script magic are precisely what make him one of the NFL’s most dangerous quarterbacks. In Buffalo’s wild 37-34 overtime win over the Rams, Allen racked up 331 total yards and two touchdowns, including a rushing score, despite throwing an interception. item.content:encoded: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has been putting on a show through the first quarter of the NFL season, making plays that few QBs can pull off. But for every highlight-reel moment, there have been a few head-scratching mistakes. Allen has racked up 15 total touchdowns this season, but he’s also coughed up the ball five times. His playmaking prowess has been a major reason behind Buffalo’s 4-1 start, but NFL fans believe the Bills superstar is getting off too easy for his costly turnovers. Why Josh Allen Gets Away With More Oct 18, 2026; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) throws in the first quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Brytus-Imagn Images The Buffalo Bills are off to a 4-1 start and are coming off a statement win over the Los Angeles Rams. But as the Bills keep stacking wins, Josh Allen’s all-too-familiar turnover problem continues to rear its ugly head. The bigger question, though, is whether Allen gets a different rulebook when it comes to criticism. While rival quarterbacks are branded overrated or have their games reduced to their rushing ability, the Bills superstar gets celebrated for his dual-threat brilliance and often gets a pass for his costly mistakes, with his supporting cast frequently entering the conversation. More so, the Bills also were against the Eagles’ famous tush-push and voted to ban it in the NFL, but in 2025, Josh Allen was one of the quarterbacks who used the tush-push the most. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ball Culture HD • Basketball • Hoops ™️ (@ballculturehd) To his credit, Allen has never shied away from owning his mistakes. The four-time MVP contender has often been his own harshest critic, taking accountability when things go sideways. But that hasn’t stopped the turnovers from becoming a recurring storyline. Take Buffalo’s Week 3 clash with the Los Angeles Chargers . Allen threw two interceptions and lost a fumble as the Bills coughed up the ball five times. Buffalo still escaped with a 24-16 win, but its defense had to step up to prevent those giveaways from turning into a late-game meltdown. The following week, Allen’s turnover bug bit again in a 29-26 loss to the New England Patriots . Trailing by three with 1:14 left on the clock, Allen escaped pressure and launched a deep ball toward Josh Palmer, only for safety Craig Woodson to come down with the game-sealing interception. Allen admitted afterward that he should have thrown the ball away. Of course, there’s another side to the story. Allen’s gunslinger mentality and off-script magic are precisely what make him one of the NFL’s most dangerous quarterbacks. In Buffalo’s wild 37-34 overtime win over the Rams, Allen racked up 331 total yards and two touchdowns, including a rushing score, despite throwing an interception. His ability to turn a busted play into a back-breaking gain helped the Bills pull off the comeback. And that’s the Josh Allen conundrum. The same improvisational flair that makes him a nightmare for opposing defenses can also put Buffalo in a hole when he tries to play hero ball. His aggressive style is a weapon, but it can become a liability when he forces throws into coverage. That’s the double-standard debate Carter is putting under the microscope: Are Allen’s mistakes judged by the same standards as those of other NFL quarterbacks, or does his superstar status buy him extra leeway? For the Bills, the answer on the field is straightforward. Allen doesn’t need to stop taking risks or dial back the playmaking that makes him special. He just needs to pick his spots better and protect the football. Because in a league where every possession matters, even an elite quarterback can’t afford to keep giving defenses extra chances. item.title: Francisco Lindor wins Roberto Clemente Award, MLB's prestigious honor
item.description: When Francisco Lindor was growing up in Puerto Rico, one of the prominent history lessons was about Roberto Clemente and the legacy he left behind. Clemente, a native of Puerto Rico, was one of the greatest baseball players of his generation, a staunch advocate for Latin American athletes, and a humanitarian with a passion for helping the less fortunate and kids through sports. Those lessons resonated with Lindor throughout his youth. Now, the New York Mets shortstop has received one of the top distinctions in Major League Baseball as he was named the 2026 recipient of the Roberto Clemente Award on Oct. 26. What Francisco Lindor says about winning Roberto Clemente Award The award has been given each year since 1971 to a player who best represents baseball through sportsmanship, community involvement and positive contributions on and off the field. "To me, this honor, this award, it's probably one of the most important awards in MLB, just because it's not about myself," Lindor said. "It's about my family, my parents, how much they have instilled in me to give and share the blessings that I have had. "And to be part of a fraternity, a community of all the recipients that have won this award, guys like (Carlos) Delgado, (Carlos) Beltran, Edgar Martinez, guys that I grew up idolizing, the Molinas. There's so many big names that represented the game the right way on the field but off the field, they were even greater." Lindor is the fifth player to receive the recognition as a member of the Mets, joining Curtis Granderson (2016), Delgado (2006), Al Leiter (2000) and Gary Carter (1989). The award brings added meaning for Lindor as a native of Puerto Rico. He credited his parents for pushing him to give back and his wife for playing a key role in their philanthropic efforts. "Hopefully this inspires another generation to continue to care for others, continue to love your neighbors, continue to love, continue to give back," Lindor said. "Sometimes us athletes can be seen like we're so far away from the general public, but we're not. We are in the communities. We are giving back and we are helping. Hopefully this is going to give me a bigger platform to continue to help and create better opportunities for people back home." Now, the New York Mets shortstop has received one of the top distinctions in Major League Baseball as he was named the 2026 recipient of the Roberto Clemente Award on Oct. 26. "To me, this honor, this award, it's probably one of the most important awards in MLB, just because it's not about myself," Lindor said. "It's about my family, my parents, how much they have instilled in me to give and share the blessings that I have had. "And to be part of a fraternity, a community of all the recipients that have won this award, guys like (Carlos) Delgado, (Carlos) Beltran, Edgar Martinez, guys that I grew up idolizing, the Molinas. There's so many big names that represented the game the right way on the field but off the field, they were even greater." Lindor is the fifth player to receive the recognition as a member of the Mets, joining Curtis Granderson (2016), Delgado (2006), Al Leiter (2000) and Gary Carter (1989). The award brings added meaning for Lindor as a native of Puerto Rico. He credited his parents for pushing him to give back and his wife for playing a key role in their philanthropic efforts. "Hopefully this inspires another generation to continue to care for others, continue to love your neighbors, continue to love, continue to give back," Lindor said. "Sometimes us athletes can be seen like we're so far away from the general public, but we're not. We are in the communities. We are giving back and we are helping. Hopefully this is going to give me a bigger platform to continue to help and create better opportunities for people back home." How Francisco Lindor is involved in the community Lindor's efforts to give back predate his time with the Mets. Since 2020, he has donated more than $1 million to develop Lindor Hall, a two-story middle school with science and technology labs, at his alma mater Monteverde Academy near Orlando, Florida. He also established a scholarship fund at the school. Along with his wife, Katia, the Lindor have partnered with the SEEN Foundation, which supports families and caregivers navigating cancer and disabilities. Lindor has done his part to bring out impacted children to the ballpark on his "Smile Tuesdays". "One of the things I'm most proud of, I would say, the SEEN thing that my wife and I are involved (with), because my kids get to be in it too," Lindor said. "They get to greet that group. I'm extremely proud of it because my kids get to experience it firsthand, and hopefully, this is just us planting the seed in their heads that this is a way of living. We are blessed and we gotta bless others, not because it's a requirement but because it's in our personalities." The Mets shortstop has also launched Lindor's Leaders, a development program centered on mental health, communication, teamwork and leadership for students in Bayside High School's sports medicine program where he mentors students. "It's more about being there for them, not just touching them one time and disappearing," Lindor said. "It's about being there and being able to have conversations with them throughout the year. That's one that I take a lot of pride in." Now, Lindor has been acknowledged as a diligent disciple of Clemente. He will receive the honor of wearing a patch of Clemente's iconic No. 21 on his hat each time he steps on the field and join the pantheon of other great MLB players who paid it forward. "It's a little bit surreal," Lindor said. "This, to me, it's bigger than baseball. We are in the entertainment business and we are there to bring smiles and joy to people but to also carry off the field. To me, it's even cooler. It's something that I'll forever continue to do." item.title: Braves Must Fix Shortstop Hole And Pitching Depth Now
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Atlanta Braves have a clear path to 2027, but two massive holes threaten to derail it. The front office faces hard choices before the winter meetings even start. We need to fix the shortstop spot and add real depth to the rotation. The numbers tell us exactly where the team broke down this year. MLB.com reported that the team received a 67 Weighted Runs Created Plus from the shortstop position. This stat means the offense at that spot was 33 percent below the league average. That is a huge problem for a team that wants to win another title. There’s also reason to be concerned about the production at third base (82 wRC+), left field (85 wRC+) and second base (85 wRC+). Shortstop is the most glaring issue on the roster. The Shortstop Dilemma Mauricio Dubón is the obvious answer to plug this gap. When he played shortstop this year, he posted a 115 wRC+ and earned a Fielding Run Value of +3. He proved he can handle the position every day while hitting the ball well. The Braves obtained him via trade after the Houston Astros designated Ramón Urías for assignment. Now, they must decide if he stays there or moves to his usual utility role. Keeping Dubón at shortstop seems like the smartest play. It fixes the biggest offensive hole, though the team must first negotiate a new contract as he is a pending free agent. He has the skills to be an everyday player there. The team should stop shuffling him around and let him own the position. This move alone could lift the entire lineup out of the basement. Rotation Depth Questions The pitching side presents challenges. Chris Sale posted a 196 Adjusted ERA, which is the third-best mark in franchise history for a pitcher with 25 starts. The only Braves to produce a better mark (min. 25 starts) in a season were Greg Maddux (271 in 1994 and 260 in 1995) and Reynaldo López (208 in 2024). Sale threw his four-seamer at 96.1 mph, his highest career average, and stayed healthy all season. The plan of giving him extra rest worked perfectly. However, the team only has three pitchers they can count on to make 25 starts. Grant Holmes, Bryce Elder, and Sale are the sole current members projected to hit that number. Reynaldo López has a right shoulder issue that will likely limit him again. Spencer Schwellenbach faces uncertainty with a screw in his elbow. If the Braves want to keep Sale fresh, they need two more starters this winter. Re-signing Tyler Mahle would be a big win, but it might not be enough. The team has young talent like AJ Smith-Shawver and JR Ritchie who have great upside. Smith-Shawver is further removed from Tommy John surgery, but he is not ready to anchor a rotation yet. The front office must look outside the organization to find reliable arms. The Cost of Inaction Ignoring these two issues will cost the Braves dearly in 2027. A shortstop who cannot hit will kill the lineup before it starts. A thin rotation will wear out Sale before October. The 2021 championship team had depth

item.title: Studs and duds from Houston’s 27-21 overtime loss against the Giants
item.description: Now it really seems like the Houston Texans are out of the playoff picture. They are two games behind the Jacksonville Jaguars despite defeating them last week. The Texans are now 2-5 on the year after their 27-21 overtime loss against the New York Giants . After putting up over 300 passing yards last week and being named the AFC Offensive Player of the Week, Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud only had 153 passing yards in this game, his fewest passing yards in a game this year and second time with under 200 passing yards. No one really stepped up in the receiving game as Houston’s leading receiver, tight end Dalton Schultz, only had five catches for 45 yards. However, there were some positives in the receiving game with Tank Dell’s return and Marvin Harrison Jr’s touchdown. On defense, the Texans struggled to contain New York’s top wide receivers, Malik Nabers and Malachi Fields, who each had over 15 yards per reception and over 80 receiving yards in the game. They also could not contain the Giants’ run game, which had season-high of 188 yards and four touchdowns. Here are the studs and duds from Houston’s loss to the Giants, including Tank Dell, who had a 43-yard reception to set up a touchdown in his return after nearly two years and Will Anderson Jr who did not play much of a factor on defense. Stud: WR Tank Dell He may have finished the game with only one catch, but it was an important play for the Texans. Dell was not even the target on the play, but capitalized on a tipped ball and turned it into 43 yards, which helped set up a touchdown just before halftime. Even if he did not have a catch, Dell would have been a stud in this game. The true victory for him is being able to return to football and get some game action. It may not have led to a win in this game, but Dell’s comeback is bigger than football. Dud: WR Nico Collins Houston’s best wide receiver this season has been Collins. However, when the Texans needed him in this game, he did not show up. Despite being targeted six times, Collins finished with just two receptions for six yards, his fewest receiving yards in a game since his rookie year in 2021. If Collins had been more involved on offense, Houston might have won. Stud: WR Marvin Harrison Jr . Like Dell, he only finished the game with one reception. However, Harrison Jr’s only reception was in the end zone for a touchdown and it was a beauty. The Texans are still working to get Harrison more involved in the offense, but it was good to see him get his first touchdown in a Texans uniform. Ironically, it is the second time he has scored a touchdown against New York; his only touchdown with the Arizona Cardinals this year was also against the Giants. Dud: DE Will Anderson Jr After starting the year with 7.5 sacks in the first five games, Anderson now has back-to-back games with no sacks. Stroud only had 153 passing yards in this game, his fewest passing yards in a game this year and second time with under 200 passing yards. It may not have led to a win in this game, but Dell’s comeback is bigger than football. Dud: WR Nico Collins Houston’s best wide receiver this season has been Collins. However, when the Texans needed him in this game, he did not show up. Despite being targeted six times, Collins finished with just two receptions for six yards, his fewest receiving yards in a game since his rookie year in 2021. However, Harrison Jr’s only reception was in the end zone for a touchdown and it was a beauty. The Texans are still working to get Harrison more involved in the offense, but it was good to see him get his first touchdown in a Texans uniform. Ironically, it is the second time he has scored a touchdown against New York; his only touchdown with the Arizona Cardinals this year was also against the Giants. Dud: DE Will Anderson Jr After starting the year with 7.5 sacks in the first five games, Anderson now has back-to-back games with no sacks. In the past two games, he has only five tackles and one solo tackle. In this game, he failed to register a quarterback hit for the first time this year. When Houston’s defense needs a big play, they go to Anderson Jr. However, he has not been showing up the past two games and it was costly this week. Stud: LB Henry To’o To’o Perhaps he was not ready to come back last week, but he was definitely ready this week. To’o To’o was second on the team in tackles with 10 and shared a sack with M.J. Stewart, who had 12 tackles in this game. He also finished this game with two tackles for loss; To’o To’o previously had just one tackle for loss this year. Houston’s defense certainly could have played better, but he had a good individual effort. Dud: WR Jaylin Noel After having a great performance last week, Noel was essentially a non-factor on offense. He finished the game with two receptions for -3 yards, his fewest receiving yards in an NFL game. Noel also only had one kick return for 21 yards and one punt return for 11 yards. Houston’s offense needed all the help they could get, and Noel was another receiver who did not show up. Stud: P Kai Kroeger Both teams combined for 10 punts, with six of them coming from the Texans. Field position became very important in this game and Kroeger gave Houston an advantage with an average of 46.2 yards per punt, one punt inside the 20-yard line and his longest punt was 55 yards. Unfortunately, the Texans were unable to capitalize on his good performance, but Kroeger did everything he possibly could in this game. Stud: CB Kamari Lassiter Lassiter had a strong performance with eight tackles, including five solo tackles. However, he also recorded his first career sack in this game. He has been in the NFL since Houston drafted him in the second round in 2024. Part of that is because the Texans do not tend to use him in blitz packages, but it worked out for them on that play. This article originally appeared on Texans Wire: Studs and duds from Houston’s 27-21 overtime loss against the Giants

item.title: JJ McCarthy compared to Super Bowl-winning QB by Colin Cowherd after Giants win
item.description: Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images JJ McCarthy helped the New York Giants to their first win with him as a starter, and he is already earning comparisons with another underrated Super Bowl-winning quarterback. McCarthy was traded from the Minnesota Vikings to the Giants just a few weeks ago, after Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending injury. And while he had to initially earn his first start over Jameis Winston, McCarthy did not disappoint when given the opportunity. Colin Cowherd says JJ McCarthy is showing shades of Sam Darnold Speaking on his podcast, Colin Cowherd drew parallels between JJ McCarthy and Sam Darnold’s careers, and questioned whether McCarthy was on the same trajectory as Darnold. He pointed out just how similar the start of both their careers had been, and questioned whether the Giants were about to benefit from having a player like McCarthy. “Is JJ McCarthy the next Sam Darnold? First-round pick, goes to an organisation and it just starts poorly, never gets going, Darnold leaves. “A lot of players wanted Darnold. Do we have a Darnold on our hands as the Giants, on the road, beat a Houston team that was favoured by 9?” What makes this connection even more interesting is the fact that Sam Darnold’s big career turnaround came thanks in large part to JJ McCarthy. McCarthy was expected to be the Minnesota Vikings’ starting quarterback, but a season-ending meniscus injury forced the Vikings to change plans. The Vikings had signed Darnold prior to drafting McCarthy with the idea of letting them compete for the starting spot, but McCarthy’s injury allowed Darnold to shine. Perhaps McCarthy could find himself in a similar situation with Jaxson Dart’s injury, where he shines with the New York Giants. item.title: Eagles vs. Cowboys Week 7 game information
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are now 2-4 heading into their Week 7 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football , and both NFC East teams desperately need a win. Expectations have changed a lot for the Eagles, whose list of injured players includes nearly half of the active 53-man roster, but this is still a rivalry game in Philadelphia on Monday night. It might not be the same as when Jalen Hurts greets the team out of the tunnel, but they are getting some guys back, including Saquon Barkley. The run game should get a big boost with Barkley back, and if C Drew Kendall and LG Landon Dickerson are both able to get back onto the field, there might be some hope for the Eagles on the ground. That would certainly help Tanner McKee as he tries to settle into his new role as the starting quarterback — a role he hopes to keep with Joe Milton also looking for an opportunity. Perhaps all the new lineups will benefit the Eagles offense this week, as they face off against their former DB coach, and current Cowboys defensive coordinator, Christian Parker. There’s barely familiarity from one week to the next, let alone from a guy who hasn’t been in Philadelphia for 10 months. Make the SB Nation app part of Eagles game day! New to Bleeding Green Nation? Perhaps all the new lineups will benefit the Eagles offense this week, as they face off against their former DB coach, and current Cowboys defensive coordinator, Christian Parker. item.title: Paris Saint-Germain are about to ruin Liverpool's transfer plans
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain are about to ruin Liverpool's transfer plans Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain have been fairly intertwined with one another over the last couple of years. The two teams have met in the Champions League knockout stages twice in a row with the Parisian's coming out on top each time. And then this summer, they were both pulled into a long and drawn out negotiation for Bradley Barcola which Liverpool eventually won. There's no signs that the relationship between the two clubs is strained but, after this latest update, that could all be about to change. Paris Saint-Germain want Gilberto Mora now that Kvicha Kvaratskhelia is out injured One of the main things that forced negotiations for Barcola's deal to drag on was the fact that Luis Enrique wanted to sign his replacement before he sold the Frenchman. Because, even though Barcola wasn't one of Enrique's main starters, he still played an important role in their plans. In the end, everything worked out with PSG managing to add Ferran Torres and Mika Godts to their squad. Each player has had a decent go at proving their worth but now, after it was confirmed that Kvicha Kvaratskhelia will be out for the rest of the 2026-27 season thanks to an ACL tear, they're an attacker down. Most clubs in this situation would deal with it and make-do but, PSG aren't like most clubs with the two-time Champions League winners now throwing their hat into the ring for the transfer of long-term Liverpool target, Gilberto Mora . "Following Khvicha Kvaratskhelia's ACL injury, PSG have stepped up their search for attacking reinforcements," Ekrem Konur wrote . "Gilberto Mora is among the players being considered by the French champions. "Liverpool are also said to have made a €40 million offer, with PSG expected to enter the race in January." Liverpool cannot let Gilberto Mora slip through their grasp One thing that Liverpool have become really good at recently is signing youngsters for the future. Many different talented players have been linked with an Anfield switch with some even having their moves confirmed. And, since Andoni Iraola is now at the helm , a lot of the Reds' youngsters are being given more frequent chances. So, the fact that they've recently been linked with a move for Mora makes a lot of sense. He set the 2026 World Cup alight and, this season, he's already contributed to five goals in seven games. The fact that he's only 18 years old means that, by the time he needs to be registered by Liverpool, he'll be classed as homegrown which is massive. Here's hoping that the Reds don't slow down their chase and manage to sign the Mexican wonderkid this summer.

item.title: WSL talking points: Russo to Arsenal’s rescue and Olid makes Manchester United progress
item.description: Gunners edged north London derby while new United manager put the brakes on Manchester City’s winning start The penalty that allowed Arsenal to come from a goal behind to take the lead may have come with a healthy helping of luck, with the ball having come off Ella Morris’s raised arm as her teammate attempted to clear it, but it could prove to be the turning point Arsenal needed. “It’s been tough. We haven’t got the results we wanted,” penalty scorer Alessia Russo told the BBC afterwards. “This was an important win as far as north London derbies goes. It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result. Suzanne Wrack Continue reading...

item.title: McTominay stars in Napoli draw that leaves Allegri ‘not lucid enough’ to talk
item.description: Gli Azzurri show positive signs of improvement in seesaw 3-3 draw against a Roma side inspired by Messi-like Matías Soulé Scott McTominay was leaving nothing to doubt. He appeared to have scored with a close-range header early in the second half of Napoli’s game at home to Roma, but Pierluigi Gollini clawed the ball out from inside the goal. McTominay got his noggin to the rebound, nudging it back across the line. Roma’s keeper pushed away again, so the Napoli midfielder got to his feet and smashed a shot into the back of the net. Just typical. You wait two months for your first goal of the Serie A season, then three show up at once. They only counted for one, of course, but McTominay looked happy enough with that as he ran to thank Matteo Politano for the assist. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Bournemouth’s transfer nous puts United to shame, Araújo is winning admirers at Anfield and Suzuki adapts swiftly at Villa The three Bournemouth goalscorers cost a combined £85m, joining from Vasco da Gama, Middlesbrough, and Porto. The Cherries are smart at investing, far more so than Manchester United, who have wasted a lot of money by failing to look outside the box for players like Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson. United may not have the wealth they previously showed in the transfer market but Bournemouth are showing what can be done within a budget and, more importantly, will be able to make a profit on signings. United, however, only know losses as everyone’s price tag diminishes the moment they come through the Old Trafford door. Jason Wilcox and others can point to certain factors that are against them but there are quality signings to be made at the right price if you have the ability to find them. item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Pierre Sage regrets ‘missed 15 minutes’ as defeat increases heat on Crystal Palace manager
item.description: Sage’s side beaten 2-0 at home by Newcastle ‘Every mistake that is bad will be a goal’ Pierre Sage blamed a 15-minute loss of concentration for Crystal Palace’s 2-0 defeat by Newcastle and insisted he remains the right man to lead the south London club. “We missed 15 minutes when we came back from the dressing room,” the Frenchman said. “When you let your opponent take the initiative without pressure, without reply, it’s difficult.” Palace have conceded 19 goals in eight games and have the worst defensive record in the Premier League, an obvious contrast to last season when Sage’s Lens side had the second-best defensive record in Ligue 1. “When we concede all these goals … you can interpret that through the style of play and also how well we are playing, especially defensively,” Sage said. Continue reading...

item.title: Fernandes gamble leaves Carrick to carry the can for United’s institutional failures | Will Unwin
item.description: Leaving out his captain was doomed to fail but so are the club under the current leadership and the fans at Old Trafford know that all too well Dropping your captain, who has held the team together for most of the past five years, is a bold move from a man whose job is on the line. It was very much a make-or-break decision from Michael Carrick to leave out Bruno Fernandes against Bournemouth. It did not work and Carrick knew the consequences if it failed and will probably pay the price for it, but he should not be alone. Carrick said the decision to drop the Portuguese playmaker was purely based on football reasons but criticising his manager after the desperate defeat to Como cannot have helped. Clearly Carrick disagreed with his captain’s comments on the lack of pressing in the Champions League fixture. It was somewhat telling that Lisandro Martínez kept his place despite pointing out the director of football, Jason Wilcox, was a hindrance to the club the previous week. Continue reading...

item.title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end
item.description: Brighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in the Premier League this season, who looked upwardly mobile. There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break. Continue reading...

item.title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews
item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
item.description: There are days when Tottenham go into these big games and find ways to beat themselves. This time, though, they held their nerve at a ground where they have mostly only known doom. Spurs played with control, stayed patient and won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018 after waiting for Chelsea to press the self-destruct button during a calamitous and comical ending to a cagey game. Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. Continue reading...

item.description: Defender costs three goals in past two league matches Emery praises ‘fantastic’ match-winner Jackson Enzo Maresca is not concerned by the form of Marc Guéhi despite the defender costing his side three goals in the past two Premier League matches, the Manchester City manager said after seeing his side lose in the league for the first time this season. Nicolas Jackson’s double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park after Guéhi was unable to control the ball for the opener. Instead he spilled it into the path of John McGinn, who played it to Jackson, allowing him to score the first of two goals. The defender was then substituted at half-time having been booked on 32 minutes. Guéhi’s errors allowed Ipswich to score twice against City last weekend. Continue reading...

The defender was then substituted at half-time having been booked on 32 minutes. Guéhi’s errors allowed Ipswich to score twice against City last weekend. Continue reading...

City are certainly fallible, losing for the fourth time in a row here, and it was a reminder that life will not always be as simple as their first seven games. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

item.title: Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start
item.description: Midfielder ‘who can never stand still’ has brought renewed energy to Seagulls since return to the club in January Most footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 , the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor. Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. item.title: Wigan pine for FA Cup glory as not even victory can lift them off foot of League One
item.description: Gary Caldwell, club captain in 2013 and now manager, needs much more than the weekend win against Reading to disperse the clouds If the 2013 FA Cup final represented a blip for the Sheikh Mansour-era Manchester City in their quest for total domination of English football, it was a historic moment for their conquerors, Wigan Athletic. Memories of that famous day at Wembley still endure for Latics supporters despite the relegation from the Premier League that followed. Yet watching the modern‑day Wigan, who remain bottom of League One despite a 1-0 win against Reading on Saturday, makes the toppling of City in a Cup final seem an epoch ago. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...
